## 6. Design

### 6.1 New scenarios

| Scenario | Shape | Served by | Declared `FinishReason` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ReasoningCleanStop` | Reasoning, then text, then one tool call, then the stop reason. | `anthropic`, from all of run C (`thinking_text_tool_use.txt`) | `ToolCalls` |
| `ParallelToolCallCleanStop` | Two or more complete tool calls, then the stop reason. | `gemini`, from `parallel_signed.sse` | `ToolCalls` |
| `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop` | One tool call with an empty argument object, then the stop reason. | `openai/responses`, from `responses_tool_call_zero_args.txt` | `ToolCalls` |

All three expect a stop reason and end with `Finish`. All three get the clean-stop floor (a
`Finish` exists and carries the declared reason). The two tool scenarios get the tool floors.

`ReasoningCleanStop` is "clean stop" in the sense of the suite: the stream ends after a stop
reason. Its name does not say `end_turn`. The only reasoning capture ends with `tool_use`, so the
scenario includes the tool call. The `anthropic` script for it keeps the text block of run C, at
index 1, and the `tool_use` at index 2. The text block emits a text-position `ProviderData` with
no `call_id` (`providers-anthropic/src/stream.rs:275-279`). Assertion 8 ignores it.

Add the three scenarios to `Scenario::ALL`, `expects_stop_reason`, `fakes::conforming`, the
`fakes::finish` reason mapping and the `declared_finish_reason` test helper.

### 6.2 New `classify` rules

These rules need no fixture knowledge, so they go in `classify` and run on every scenario.

**Assertion 9: nothing after `Err`** (G1). Any event, `Ok` or `Err`, after the first `Err` is a
violation: `Violation::EventAfterError`, with one exception: a `Usage` after an `Err` is allowed
(§6.6, option B). Order inside `classify`: after assertion 6 (`FinishAfterError`), so that the
more specific name wins for a `Finish` after an `Err`. A positive test shows that `Err, Usage`
passes.

**Assertion 10: tool arguments parse as JSON** (G4). Runs only when the stream contains a
`Finish`. A truncated, errored or cancelled stream can correctly end in the middle of the
arguments, and a consumer calls `finish()` only after a `Finish`. For each `call_id` group,
concatenate the `args_delta`s in stream order. Blank or whitespace-only becomes `{}`. The result
must parse as a JSON value: `Violation::ToolArgsNotJson { call_id }`. This is the accumulator's
rule (§3.4). A blank-`call_id` group is checked only when it carries exactly one name. With two
or more names, the group holds several calls, and the accumulator refuses that turn anyway
(SMA-621). Assertion 10 runs on every tool scenario for every subject, so it also covers the
existing fixtures. All existing served fixtures pass it today.

### 6.3 New floor checks

These checks need fixture knowledge, so they go in `floor_violation`, the same as the existing
`FinishReasonMismatch` check. The existing rule of `floor_violation` stays: a floor reports only
missing evidence, or a mismatch with a declaration. It leaves the exact diagnosis to `classify`.

**No `Err` outside the error scenarios.** In every scenario except `ErrorMidGeneration` and
`ErrorAfterStopReason`, the stream must yield no `Err`. Today, nothing stops a clean script from
being read as an error. This floor closes the SMA-533 §6 statement that S3 "will not be
mis-reported as S4a".

**`CleanStop` yields a `Usage`.** Every `CleanStop` script carries usage, so a stream without
`Usage` did not serve the scenario's bytes.

**Channel order** (G2). A new trait method declares the run order of the fixture for a scenario:

```rust
/// One run of same-channel events, in wire order.
pub enum Channel { Reasoning, Text, Tool }

fn fixture_channel_order(&self, scenario: Scenario) -> Option<&'static [Channel]>;
```

`None` means "no claim". For `ReasoningCleanStop`, the subject must return `Some(..)`. If it
returns `None`, the floor fails with `InsufficientEvidence`. The check maps each `ReasoningDelta`,
`TokenDelta` and `ToolCallDelta` to its channel, ignores all other events, merges adjacent equal
channels into one run, and compares the result with the declared order:
`Violation::ChannelOrderMismatch { expected, observed }`. A further floor for `ReasoningCleanStop`
requires at least one `ReasoningDelta`.

The contract lets the three channels interleave freely (`core/src/model.rs:56-57`). This check is
therefore about fidelity to the wire order, not about the contract. Its doc comment says so. An
empty delta still counts as a run. Run A shows that a real wire can carry an empty
`thinking_delta`, and the translator passes it on as an empty `ReasoningDelta`.

The `anthropic` declaration for `ReasoningCleanStop` is `[Reasoning, Text, Tool]`, read from run C.

**Declared calls** (G3, G4). A new trait method declares the calls in the fixture:

```rust
/// A tool call the fixture carries: its name and its complete arguments as JSON text.
pub struct ExpectedCall { pub name: &'static str, pub args: &'static str }

fn fixture_calls(&self, scenario: Scenario) -> &'static [ExpectedCall];
```

`args` is a `&'static str` so that the table can be a `const`. The floor parses it.
`fixture_calls` must return a non-empty list for `ParallelToolCallCleanStop` and
`ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop`, and an empty list for every other scenario. The existing tool
scenarios keep `fixture_tool_name`, which does not change. For the two new scenarios, the
"declared name is present" floor reads the names from `fixture_calls`. So the Gemini names
(`search`, `weather`) and the zero-argument name (`get_current_time`) need no change to
`fixture_tool_name`.

For both new scenarios:

- the observed calls, in first-seen `call_id` order, must equal the declared calls by name and by
  parsed arguments: `Violation::ToolCallsMismatch { expected, observed }`;
- a call whose arguments do not parse is skipped by this floor, so that assertion 10 reports it
  with its exact name;
- the match is by position, not by `call_id`, because a subject cannot always declare the ids
  that its translator makes.

For `ParallelToolCallCleanStop`, a further floor requires two or more distinct non-blank
`call_id`s. For `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop`, the declared call is `get_current_time` with arguments
`{}`. So a fixture with real arguments fails the floor, and the scenario cannot pass vacuously.

1	//! Cross-provider conformance suite for the `Model::invoke` stream
2	//! event-ordering contract.
3	//!
4	//! This internal (never-published) crate hosts a provider-agnostic checker and
5	//! a paced HTTP server. Each subject in `tests/conformance.rs` serves its own
6	//! captured wire bytes through that server and hands back the stream from its
7	//! real `Model::invoke`, so the suite exercises the production driver and the
8	//! production translator together — not a reimplementation of either.
9	//!
10	//! See `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-19-sma-533-stream-conformance-design.md`.
11	#![forbid(unsafe_code)]
12	
13	mod check;
14	mod declines;
15	pub mod eventstream;
16	#[cfg(test)]
17	mod fakes;
18	mod server;
19	
20	pub use check::classify;
21	pub use declines::{DECLINED, UNCAPTURED};
22	pub use server::{Ending, PacedServer, Script};
23	
24	use std::time::Duration;
25	
26	use futures_util::stream::{BoxStream, StreamExt};
27	use paigasus_helikon_core::{CancellationToken, FinishReason, ModelError, ModelEvent};

29	/// One wire script, run against every subject that can express it.
30	///
31	/// The `a`/`b` pairs differ only in whether the script lets the translator
32	/// observe a stop reason before the stream ends. That distinction is the whole
33	/// point: with no stop reason buffered there is nothing for a broken driver to
34	/// wrongly flush, so the `a` variants cannot fail assertions 5 and 6 on their
35	/// own.
36	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
37	pub enum Scenario {
38	    /// Deltas, stop reason, usage, terminator, clean EOF.
39	    CleanStop,
40	    /// Stop reason observed, then the body ends cleanly with no terminator.
41	    TruncatedAfterStopReason,
42	    /// Body ends cleanly mid-generation; no stop reason is ever observed.
43	    TruncatedMidGeneration,
44	    /// Body aborted mid-generation; no stop reason is ever observed.
45	    ErrorMidGeneration,
46	    /// Stop reason observed, then the body is aborted.
47	    ErrorAfterStopReason,
48	    /// Cancelled mid-generation; no stop reason is ever observed.
49	    CancelMidGeneration,
50	    /// Stop reason observed, then cancelled before end-of-stream.
51	    CancelAfterStopReason,
52	    /// A tool call whose name arrives split across two or more deltas.
53	    FragmentedToolName,
54	    /// One complete tool call followed by a tool-use stop reason.
55	    ToolCallCleanStop,
56	    /// A signed thinking block, then one complete tool call, then a tool-use
57	    /// stop reason.
58	    ThinkingToolCallCleanStop,
59	    /// Reasoning, then text, then one complete tool call, then a tool-use
60	    /// stop reason. Provider-neutral: any reasoning channel serves it.
61	    ReasoningCleanStop,
62	}
63	
64	impl Scenario {
65	    /// Every scenario, in table order.
66	    pub const ALL: &'static [Scenario] = &[
67	        Scenario::CleanStop,
68	        Scenario::TruncatedAfterStopReason,
69	        Scenario::TruncatedMidGeneration,
70	        Scenario::ErrorMidGeneration,
71	        Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason,
72	        Scenario::CancelMidGeneration,
73	        Scenario::CancelAfterStopReason,
74	        Scenario::FragmentedToolName,
75	        Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop,
76	        Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop,
77	        Scenario::ReasoningCleanStop,
78	    ];
79	
80	    /// Whether this scenario's script must let the translator observe a stop
81	    /// reason. Cross-checked against each subject's own declaration so a
82	    /// mis-transcribed fixture cannot make assertion 3 pass vacuously.
83	    pub fn expects_stop_reason(self) -> bool {
84	        matches!(
85	            self,
86	            Scenario::CleanStop
87	                | Scenario::TruncatedAfterStopReason
88	                | Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason
89	                | Scenario::CancelAfterStopReason
90	                | Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop
91	                | Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop
92	                | Scenario::ReasoningCleanStop
93	        )
94	    }
95	}

97	/// One run of same-channel events, in wire order.
98	///
99	/// `ReasoningDelta`, `TokenDelta` and `ToolCallDelta` each map to one channel.
100	/// Adjacent events of one channel merge into one run.
101	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
102	pub enum Channel {
103	    /// `ReasoningDelta` events.
104	    Reasoning,
105	    /// `TokenDelta` events.
106	    Text,
107	    /// `ToolCallDelta` events.
108	    Tool,
109	}
110	
111	/// A contract violation, classified. Ordering matters — see `classify`.
112	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
113	pub enum Violation {
114	    /// More than one `Finish` was emitted (assertion 1).
115	    DuplicateFinish,
116	    /// A `Usage` was emitted after `Finish` (assertion 2).
117	    UsageAfterFinish,
118	    /// Any other event, or an `Err`, was emitted after `Finish` (assertion 1).
119	    EventAfterFinish,
120	    /// End-of-stream after an observed stop reason emitted no `Finish`
121	    /// (assertion 3).
122	    MissingFinish,
123	    /// A `Finish` was emitted although no stop reason was observed
124	    /// (assertion 4).
125	    FinishOnTruncation,
126	    /// A `Finish` was emitted after cancellation (assertion 5).
127	    FinishOnCancel,
128	    /// A `Finish` was emitted after a mid-stream error (assertion 6).
129	    FinishAfterError,
130	    /// An event other than `Usage` followed the first `Err` (assertion 9).
131	    EventAfterError,
132	    /// A `call_id` carried a number of name-bearing deltas other than one, or
133	    /// the name did not match the fixture's declared tool name (assertion 7).
134	    ToolNameNotExactlyOnce {
135	        /// The call whose name emission was wrong.
136	        call_id: String,
137	        /// How many deltas for that `call_id` carried `Some(name)`.
138	        count: usize,
139	    },
140	    /// A `ProviderData` event named a `call_id` for which the stream carried no
141	    /// `ToolCallDelta` (assertion 8).
142	    ProviderDataUnknownCall {
143	        /// The `call_id` that no streamed tool call used.
144	        call_id: String,
145	    },
146	    /// A call's concatenated `args_delta` did not parse as JSON on a stream
147	    /// that carried a `Finish` (assertion 10).
148	    ToolArgsNotJson {
149	        /// The call whose arguments did not parse.
150	        call_id: String,
151	    },
152	    /// The stream did not produce the minimum evidence its scenario requires,
153	    /// so the assertions would have passed vacuously.
154	    InsufficientEvidence(&'static str),
155	    /// The terminal event carried a different `FinishReason` than the
156	    /// subject's fixture declares, so the bytes served are not the ones the
157	    /// scenario describes (spec §7.1).
158	    FinishReasonMismatch {
159	        /// What the subject's `fixture_finish_reason` declared.
160	        expected: FinishReason,
161	        /// What the stream actually emitted.
162	        observed: FinishReason,
163	    },
164	    /// The run order of the reasoning, text and tool channels differs from
165	    /// the order that the subject's fixture declares. This is a check of
166	    /// fidelity to the wire, not of the contract, which lets the channels
167	    /// interleave freely.
168	    ChannelOrderMismatch {
169	        /// What the subject's `fixture_channel_order` declared.
170	        expected: Vec<Channel>,
171	        /// The runs the stream actually emitted.
172	        observed: Vec<Channel>,
173	    },
174	    /// The stream did not terminate within the per-scenario timeout.
175	    Timeout,
176	    /// The subject's `encodes_stop_reason` disagreed with the scenario's own
177	    /// expectation, so its fixture does not match the script it claims.
178	    StopReasonDeclarationMismatch {
179	        /// What the scenario requires.
180	        expected: bool,
181	        /// What the subject declared.
182	        declared: bool,
183	    },
184	}
185	
186	/// Released by the harness once it has observed the gate event, letting the
187	/// server send the remaining chunks.
188	pub struct GateHandle {
189	    /// Signalled by the harness; the server waits on the paired receiver.
190	    /// Named `tx` rather than `release` so it does not shadow the method below.
191	    pub(crate) tx: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<()>,
192	}
193	
194	impl GateHandle {
195	    /// Let the server send the remaining chunks.
196	    ///
197	    /// Returns whether the server was still parked on this gate. `false` means
198	    /// it had already run its script to the end, so nothing was being withheld
199	    /// — which is how a cancellation scenario silently degrades into an ungated
200	    /// one, and why `assert_conforms` reads this value rather than discarding
201	    /// it.
202	    pub fn release(self) -> bool {
203	        self.tx.send(()).is_ok()
204	    }
205	}
206	
207	/// What a subject did with a scenario.
208	///
209	/// Declining and being uncaptured are first-class outcomes carrying a mandatory
210	/// reason, not an `Option` a caller can silently treat as a skip. Neither is
211	/// served, so no floor or assertion runs for them. The two are not
212	/// interchangeable: [`Outcome::Declined`] must match [`DECLINED`], and
213	/// [`Outcome::Uncaptured`] must match [`UNCAPTURED`].
214	pub enum Outcome {
215	    /// The subject served the scenario.
216	    Served {
217	        /// The stream returned by the subject's `Model::invoke`.
218	        stream: BoxStream<'static, Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>,
219	        /// Present only for the cancellation scenarios.
220	        gate: Option<GateHandle>,
221	    },
222	    /// The wire shape cannot physically occur for this provider. The reason is
223	    /// printed in the report and must match the pinned decline set.
224	    Declined(&'static str),
225	    /// The wire shape can occur for this provider, and a capture alone would
226	    /// let the subject serve it, but no fixture that meets the provenance rule
227	    /// exists. The reason must match the pinned [`UNCAPTURED`] table.
228	    Uncaptured(&'static str),
229	}
230	
231	/// One provider backend under test.
232	#[async_trait::async_trait]
233	pub trait StreamUnderTest {
234	    /// Stable subject name, e.g. `"openai/chat"`. Used in failure output and to
235	    /// match rows in the pinned decline set.
236	    fn name(&self) -> &'static str;
237	
238	    /// Whether this subject's fixture for `scenario` encodes a stop reason.
239	    /// Cross-checked against the scenario's own expectation.
240	    fn encodes_stop_reason(&self, scenario: Scenario) -> bool;
241	
242	    /// The tool name this subject's tool-call fixtures declare.
243	    fn fixture_tool_name(&self) -> &'static str;
244	
245	    /// The `FinishReason` this subject's fixture for `scenario` declares, or
246	    /// `None` for scenarios that must not produce a `Finish` at all.
247	    ///
248	    /// Exactly five scenarios end with a `Finish`, and the floor checks this
249	    /// value for all five: `CleanStop`, `ToolCallCleanStop`,
250	    /// `ThinkingToolCallCleanStop`, `ReasoningCleanStop`, and
251	    /// `TruncatedAfterStopReason`, where assertion 3 requires the buffered
252	    /// stop reason to be flushed at end-of-stream. Every other scenario must
253	    /// return `None` — a cancelled or errored stream withholds `Finish`, and a
254	    /// truncation with no stop reason observed never had one to emit.
255	    ///
256	    /// The five differ in one way only: for the four clean stops a missing
257	    /// `Finish` fails the floor, whereas for `TruncatedAfterStopReason` it is
258	    /// `classify`'s `MissingFinish` (the SMA-531 shape). Either way, a `Finish`
259	    /// that *is* emitted must carry what this method declares.
260	    ///
261	    /// Declared per subject rather than inferred suite-side because only the
262	    /// fixture knows what its bytes encode: a checker that assumed
263	    /// `CleanStop` ⇒ `Stop` would silently accept a fixture that had been
264	    /// transcribed with the wrong stop reason.
265	    fn fixture_finish_reason(&self, scenario: Scenario) -> Option<FinishReason>;
266	
267	    /// The run order of the reasoning, text and tool channels in this
268	    /// subject's fixture for `scenario`, read from the capture. `None` means
269	    /// that the subject makes no claim.
270	    ///
271	    /// `ReasoningCleanStop` requires `Some(..)`. For any scenario that returns
272	    /// `Some(..)`, the floor compares the observed runs with it.
273	    fn fixture_channel_order(&self, scenario: Scenario) -> Option<&'static [Channel]>;
274	
275	    /// Serve `scenario` and return the subject's `Model::invoke` stream.
276	    async fn stream(&self, scenario: Scenario, cancel: CancellationToken) -> Outcome;
277	}
278	
279	/// How long one scenario's drain may run before the suite gives up on it.
280	///
281	/// A subject whose stream never terminates is a real bug this suite should
282	/// catch, and without a bound it would hang `cargo test` rather than fail it.
283	/// Generous on purpose: it is only ever reached on failure, so it costs nothing
284	/// on a green run.
285	const DRAIN_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10);
286	
287	/// How long a gated stream must stay silent before the harness accepts that the
288	/// server is parked on the gate and fires cancellation.
289	///
290	/// **Why quiescence and not a named gate edge.** The design spec's §6.1 has the
291	/// harness block on a specific event — a `TokenDelta` for `CancelMidGeneration`,
292	/// the `Usage` the fixture places after the stop-reason chunk for
293	/// `CancelAfterStopReason`. That does not survive contact with Anthropic, which
294	/// emits a `Usage` from `message_start` (`anthropic/stream.rs:79`): "cancel on
295	/// the first `Usage`" would fire before any stop reason was buffered, and
296	/// `CancelAfterStopReason` would silently degrade into `CancelMidGeneration` for
297	/// that subject. Silence is subject-independent, and — unlike an event
298	/// predicate — is itself positive evidence that the server is withholding.
299	///
300	/// **What a slow machine does to it.** Firing *late* (the harness task is
301	/// descheduled, so the window elapses later in wall-clock terms) is harmless:
302	/// the server is parked either way and nothing else is in flight. Firing
303	/// *early* is the dangerous direction, and the timer arms twice with different
304	/// stakes:
305	///
306	/// - **Between two events.** Needs two consecutive pre-gate chunks more than
307	///   this far apart, which the server does not produce: `feed` pushes every
308	///   pre-gate chunk into an unbounded channel with no await between them, so
309	///   they reach the socket back-to-back over loopback. If it ever did happen,
310	///   the consequence is a weaker test — cancellation at an earlier truncation
311	///   point — not a red run.
312	/// - **Before the first event**, which is the arming that can actually fail a
313	///   run. It covers connect, request, response head and first chunk, with
314	///   nothing yet consumed. Should *that* window elapse, the token fires having
315	///   collected nothing and the scenario dies on the "no TokenDelta" floor — a
316	///   spurious failure, not a weaker test. Sub-millisecond on loopback, but it
317	///   is the first thing to suspect behind an intermittent cancel-scenario
318	///   failure, ahead of anything in the provider.
319	///
320	/// The `server_was_parked` evidence below is unaffected in every case.
321	const GATE_QUIESCENCE: Duration = Duration::from_millis(400);
322	
323	/// Run every [`Scenario`] against `subject` and panic on the first thing that
324	/// does not hold.
325	///
326	/// Three guards run in order for each served scenario, and each exists because
327	/// of a specific way this suite could go quietly useless:
328	///
329	/// 1. **The stop-reason declaration is cross-checked.** Assertions 3 and 4 are
330	///    conditioned on whether a stop reason was observed, and that cannot be
331	///    inferred from the emitted events — a provider wrongly suppressing
332	///    `Finish` looks identical to one that correctly never saw a stop reason.
333	/// 2. **The positive-evidence floors run before the assertions.** A stream that
334	///    emits nothing satisfies "ends with `Finish`" trivially, so a miswired
335	///    adapter serving the wrong fixture would otherwise pass every assertion by
336	///    producing nothing at all.
337	/// 3. **Then, and only then, the events are classified** by the crate's
338	///    `classify` function.
339	///
340	/// Afterwards the observed declines and uncaptured pairs are compared against
341	/// the pinned [`DECLINED`] and [`UNCAPTURED`] tables in both directions.
342	pub async fn assert_conforms(subject: &impl StreamUnderTest) {
343	    assert_conforms_with(subject, DECLINED, UNCAPTURED).await;
344	}
345	
346	/// [`assert_conforms`] against explicit pinned tables, so the unit tests can
347	/// drive the stale-row direction without a real row.
348	async fn assert_conforms_with(
349	    subject: &impl StreamUnderTest,
350	    pinned_declined: &[(&str, Scenario, &str)],
351	    pinned_uncaptured: &[(&str, Scenario, &str, &str)],
352	) {
353	    let name = subject.name();
354	    let mut declined: Vec<(Scenario, &'static str)> = Vec::new();
355	    let mut uncaptured: Vec<(Scenario, &'static str)> = Vec::new();
356	
357	    for &scenario in Scenario::ALL {
358	        let cancel = CancellationToken::new();
359	        let (stream, gate) = match subject.stream(scenario, cancel.clone()).await {
360	            Outcome::Declined(reason) => {
361	                declined.push((scenario, reason));
362	                continue;
363	            }
364	            Outcome::Uncaptured(reason) => {
365	                uncaptured.push((scenario, reason));
366	                continue;
367	            }
368	            Outcome::Served { stream, gate } => (stream, gate),
369	        };
370	
371	        let declared = subject.encodes_stop_reason(scenario);
372	        let expected = scenario.expects_stop_reason();
373	        if declared != expected {
374	            fail(
375	                name,
376	                scenario,
377	                &Violation::StopReasonDeclarationMismatch { expected, declared },
378	                "the subject's fixture does not encode what this scenario requires, so \
379	                 assertions 3 and 4 would be checked against the wrong condition",
380	            );
381	        }
382	
383	        let cancelled = is_cancel_scenario(scenario);
384	        if cancelled && gate.is_none() {
385	            fail(
386	                name,
387	                scenario,
388	                &Violation::InsufficientEvidence(
389	                    "a cancellation scenario was served without a gate, so the whole body was \
390	                     already on its way and cancellation could not truncate anything",
391	                ),
392	                "give the script a `gate_after` and hand the `GateHandle` back in \
393	                 `Outcome::Served`",
394	            );
395	        }
396	
397	        let Ok(drained) =
398	            tokio::time::timeout(DRAIN_TIMEOUT, drain(stream, gate, scenario, cancel)).await
399	        else {
400	            fail(
401	                name,
402	                scenario,
403	                &Violation::Timeout,
404	                "the stream never ended. For a cancellation scenario, check that the driver \
405	                 selects on the cancellation token while awaiting the next chunk; otherwise \
406	                 check that the script's ending actually closes the body",
407	            );
408	        };
409	
410	        if let Some(violation) = floor_violation(
411	            scenario,
412	            &drained.events,
413	            subject.fixture_tool_name(),
414	            subject.fixture_finish_reason(scenario),
415	            subject.fixture_channel_order(scenario),
416	        ) {
417	            fail(
418	                name,
419	                scenario,
420	                &violation,
421	                &format!("observed: {}", summarise(&drained.events)),
422	            );
423	        }
424	
425	        if let Some(violation) = drained.cancel_violation() {
426	            fail(
427	                name,
428	                scenario,
429	                &violation,
430	                &format!("observed: {}", summarise(&drained.events)),
431	            );
432	        }
433	
434	        if let Some(violation) = classify(&drained.events, scenario, cancelled) {
435	            fail(
436	                name,
437	                scenario,
438	                &violation,
439	                &format!("observed: {}", summarise(&drained.events)),
440	            );
441	        }
442	    }
443	
444	    let expected_declined: Vec<(Scenario, &str)> = pinned_declined
445	        .iter()
446	        .filter(|(n, _, _)| *n == name)
447	        .map(|(_, sc, r)| (*sc, *r))
448	        .collect();
449	    let expected_uncaptured: Vec<(Scenario, &str)> = pinned_uncaptured
450	        .iter()
451	        .filter(|(n, _, _, _)| *n == name)
452	        .map(|(_, sc, r, _)| (*sc, *r))
453	        .collect();
454	
455	    let mut problems = pinned_problems(PinnedKind::Declined, &declined, &expected_declined);
456	    problems.extend(pinned_problems(
457	        PinnedKind::Uncaptured,
458	        &uncaptured,
459	        &expected_uncaptured,
460	    ));
461	    assert!(
462	        problems.is_empty(),
463	        "conformance: {name} — the observed decline or uncaptured set does not match the \
464	         pinned DECLINED or UNCAPTURED table (spec §6.2, §6.4):\n{}",
465	        problems.join("\n")
466	    );
467	}
468	
469	/// Whether `scenario` cancels the stream part-way through.
470	fn is_cancel_scenario(scenario: Scenario) -> bool {
471	    matches!(
472	        scenario,
473	        Scenario::CancelMidGeneration | Scenario::CancelAfterStopReason
474	    )
475	}
476	
477	/// Everything one scenario's drain observed.
478	struct Drained {
479	    /// The events the subject's stream produced, in order.
480	    events: Vec<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>,
481	    /// Present only for a cancellation scenario.
482	    cancel: Option<CancelEvidence>,
483	}
484	
485	/// Proof that a cancellation scenario actually cancelled something.
486	///
487	/// Dropping a [`GateHandle`] releases the body, so a cancellation scenario can
488	/// silently degrade into an ungated one — the whole script plays out, the
489	/// stream ends on its own, and the assertions pass without cancellation ever
490	/// having been exercised. Both fields below are recorded so that degradation
491	/// fails loudly instead.
492	struct CancelEvidence {
493	    /// The stream fell quiet, so the harness fired the cancellation token.
494	    /// `false` means the stream ended by itself first.
495	    fired: bool,
496	    /// The server was still parked on the gate when the stream ended, so the
497	    /// rest of the script was never delivered.
498	    server_was_parked: bool,
499	}
500	
501	impl Drained {
502	    /// The missing-evidence violation for a cancellation scenario, if any.
503	    fn cancel_violation(&self) -> Option<Violation> {
504	        let evidence = self.cancel.as_ref()?;
505	        if !evidence.fired {
506	            return Some(Violation::InsufficientEvidence(
507	                "the stream ended on its own before cancellation was fired, so this scenario \
508	                 tested no cancellation at all",
509	            ));
510	        }
511	        if !evidence.server_was_parked {
512	            return Some(Violation::InsufficientEvidence(
513	                "the server had already run its script to the end when the stream finished, so \
514	                 cancellation truncated nothing",
515	            ));
516	        }
517	        None
518	    }
519	}
520	
521	/// Drain one scenario's stream, cancelling part-way through when the scenario
522	/// calls for it.
523	///
524	/// For a cancellation scenario the sequence is: read every event the server
525	/// sent before the gate; wait for the stream to fall quiet, which is what
526	/// proves the server is withholding; fire the token; read whatever the driver
527	/// still emits; and only then release the gate — the release is what reports
528	/// whether the server really was parked on it.
529	///
530	/// The gate is deliberately *not* released before cancelling. Releasing first
531	/// would put the rest of the script on the wire in a race with the token, so a
532	/// correct driver could emit `Finish` from an already-delivered terminator
533	/// before it ever observed the cancellation, and the suite would report
534	/// `FinishOnCancel` against provider code that did nothing wrong.
535	async fn drain(
536	    mut stream: BoxStream<'static, Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>,
537	    gate: Option<GateHandle>,
538	    scenario: Scenario,
539	    cancel: CancellationToken,
540	) -> Drained {
541	    let mut events = Vec::new();

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this is

The Paigasus AI SDK (codename **Helikon**, after Mt Helicon where Pegasus's hoof struck the Hippocrene spring). A Rust SDK for building AI agents. All crates live under the `paigasus-helikon-*` namespace.

The full architectural reference lives in Notion: ["Crate Reference"](https://www.notion.so/355830e8fbaa813c92e8c1aa9985fd3f). Linear project: `Paigasus Helikon` (issues prefixed `SMA-`).

## Common commands

```bash
cargo build --workspace                              # all 14 crates
cargo build --workspace --all-features               # facade with every optional crate
cargo run -p paigasus-helikon-cli --bin helikon
cargo run -p paigasus-helikon-cli --bin paigasus-helikon
```

To reproduce **every** CI gate locally (matches `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job-for-job):

```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --all-features
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps
DOC_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD=80 NIGHTLY_CHANNEL=nightly-2026-05-01 \
  bash scripts/check-doc-coverage.sh                 # requires: rustup toolchain install nightly-2026-05-01
npm ci                                               # once, or after package-lock.json changes
npx markdownlint-cli2                                # reads .markdownlint-cli2.jsonc
bash scripts/check-markdownlint-config.sh            # asserts that config is in force
bash scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync.sh         # cargo-visible workflow env is uniform
bash scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync-selftest.sh # …and its parser still parses (fmt runs both)
bash scripts/check-release-gaps-selftest.sh            # release gap report + release-plz.yml guards (fmt runs it)
bash scripts/check-breaking-cascade-selftest.sh      # the cascade guard keeps its rule (fmt runs it)
bash scripts/check-breaking-cascade.sh                 # breaking bump needs breaking dependents (PR only; fmt runs it)
```

The full list lives in `CONTRIBUTING.md` (single source of truth for contributor policies).

## Workspace layout

15 crates under `crates/`. The facade `paigasus-helikon` re-exports `paigasus-helikon-core` unconditionally and the other 12 sibling crates behind Cargo features.

Every crate carries a real implementation and publishes to crates.io; zero name-claim stubs remain (first published in SMA-385, last ascends in SMA-333). One standing exception: `paigasus-helikon-cli` publishes as a **binary** crate — its lib target is internal (`missing_docs` opted out), carries no stability guarantee, and exists only so `cargo install paigasus-helikon-cli` resolves. `paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit` publishes as a normal library crate (SMA-805); the three session backends keep a path-only dev-dependency on it. Exact versions move every release — read each crate's `Cargo.toml`, don't trust numbers written here.

Workspace inheritance is **mandatory**: per-crate `Cargo.toml`s only set `name`, `description`, and any crate-specific bits. Everything else (`edition`, `rust-version`, `authors`, `license`, `repository`, `homepage`, `keywords`, `categories`) inherits from `[workspace.package]` in the root `Cargo.toml`. Don't hardcode these per-crate.

**Per-crate version is the one exception.** No stubs remain, so the 4-step ascend recipe is now historical — but two caveats still bite any PR that hand-bumps a version:

- **If a crate uses `paigasus-helikon-core` API added in the *same* PR, bump `core` too**, along with its `[workspace.dependencies]` pin and CHANGELOG. `cargo publish --verify` builds the tarball against the **registry** core, so otherwise the publish fails and release-plz deadlocks.
- **Any PR that hand-bumps a sibling must ALSO bump the facade** (`crates/paigasus-helikon/Cargo.toml` version + its self-pin + CHANGELOG). release-plz does not bump the facade for a sibling version that is already at target when the PR merges, so a manual bump silently leaves the facade advertising stale dep reqs. (`dependencies_update = true` only makes the release PR run `cargo update` on `Cargo.lock`; it does not cascade version bumps.)
- **A breaking bump of a crate needs a breaking bump of each crate that depends on it.** release-plz gives a dependent without its own commits only a patch bump (release-plz#1599), and users then get two copies of the crate. The `fmt` job runs `scripts/check-breaking-cascade.sh` to enforce this. See `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md` → "A breaking change in a crate with dependents".
- Feature branches must match the `branch-names` ruleset (`feature/**` or `hotfix/**`); a `chore/**` branch is rejected at push with `GH013 … creations being restricted`.

Full lifecycle, the 4-step recipe, and the SMA-321/SMA-346 postmortems: `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md`.

Third-party version pins live in `[workspace.dependencies]` (root). Members reference them via `dep.workspace = true`. Internal crate paths are also in `[workspace.dependencies]` so the facade can use `workspace = true` consistently.

## Non-obvious patterns to preserve

- **Feature naming**: kebab-case in `[features]` (`runtime-tokio`), snake-case in `pub use` aliases (`runtime_tokio`). They must stay paired across the facade's `Cargo.toml` and `src/lib.rs`.
- **`paigasus-helikon-cli` uses `autobins = false`** because the `paigasus-helikon` (hyphen) binary maps to `src/bin/paigasus_helikon.rs` (underscore — hyphens are illegal in Rust filenames). Removing `autobins = false` reintroduces a phantom `paigasus_helikon` binary that conflicts with the explicit `[[bin]]` entry.
- **`paigasus-helikon-macros` is a proc-macro crate from day one** (`[lib] proc-macro = true`). Don't convert it to a regular lib even though it currently has no macros.
- **The `paigasus-helikon` facade lib shares its name with the `paigasus-helikon` CLI binary by design** (Notion ref's "fully-qualified shim alias"). This produces a non-fatal `cargo doc` filename-collision warning. Don't "fix" it by renaming either — both names are user-facing API. The accepted future fix is `doc = false` on the CLI binary entry.
- **License is dual `Apache-2.0 OR MIT`** (decided 2026-05-20, reversing the 2026-05-16 MIT-only call). Both `LICENSE-APACHE` and `LICENSE-MIT` live at the repo root; the workspace metadata is `license = "Apache-2.0 OR MIT"`. Per Rust ecosystem convention — no Apache-only or MIT-only crates in the workspace. Contributions are accepted under the same dual license by default (the standard inbound-equals-outbound clause is restated in `README.md`).
- **MSRV is `1.94`** (workspace-package level; raised from 1.85 in SMA-329 because sqlx 0.9.0 declares `rust-version = "1.94.0"` — the pre-existing highest floor in the workspace). If a dep raises MSRV, bump `rust-version` to what cargo demands rather than downgrading the dep.
- **Workspace-wide `missing_docs` enforcement** lives in root `Cargo.toml` (`[workspace.lints.rust] missing_docs = "warn"`). Each non-CLI crate opts in with `[lints] workspace = true`. The CLI overrides locally with `[lints.rust] missing_docs = "allow"` and does **not** include `workspace = true` — cargo treats `[lints] workspace = true` and an inline `[lints.<tool>]` table as mutually exclusive. When adding a new crate, copy the opt-in block. When adding a new `pub use` re-export to the facade, give it a `///` doc comment or `-D warnings` will fail the docs job.
- **`cargo msrv` has no `--workspace` flag.** The msrv workflow verifies one representative inheriting crate: `cargo msrv --path crates/paigasus-helikon-core verify`. Because every member uses `rust-version.workspace = true`, success on one is success on all. Don't "fix" the workflow by adding `--workspace`; that's what the first SMA-305 CI run died on.
- **Nightly is date-pinned** (`NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN: nightly-2026-05-01` at the workflow `env:` level in `ci.yml`, threaded into the doc-coverage script as `NIGHTLY_CHANNEL`). The rustdoc JSON coverage format is `-Z unstable-options` and can shift between nightlies; floating `nightly` would be a CI footgun. Bumping is a one-line follow-up chore, not an emergency.
- **Bootstrap commits on release infrastructure must use `chore(...)` or `docs(...)` types**, never `feat`/`fix`. release-plz parses every commit since the last per-crate tag — a `feat(workspace): ...` commit that touches every `Cargo.toml` would attribute a bump to every crate. The SMA-307 bootstrap PR followed this rule; the same rule applies to any future `release-plz.toml` or `release-plz.yml` edits.

## Workflow conventions

- Branch per Linear issue: `feature/<sma-####>-<kebab-title>`. The branch name is pre-computed in each Linear ticket's `gitBranchName` field.
- Design artifacts per ticket (`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md`) land on the feature branch alongside the implementation — not pre-merged to `main`.
- **Keep the public mdBook (`docs/book/`) current — update it in the same PR as any user-facing change.** Before opening a PR, check whether the work changes public API, the quickstart/example flow, the crate roster (incl. a stub crate ascending to published), or a documented concept; if so, bring the affected `docs/book/src/*.md` page(s) into line on the same branch. The book is published from `main` and drifts silently otherwise — it sat as the untouched SMA-311 scaffold (13/17 pages still `> **Stub.**`) through all of Stage 1 before anyone noticed; SMA-423 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no book edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip. `mdbook build docs/book` must stay clean (`[output.linkcheck] warning-policy = "error"`).
- **Keep crate `README.md` files current — update the affected crate's README in the same PR as any change to its public surface.** Each of the ten published crates' `README.md` is its crates.io (and docs.rs landing-sidebar) page — no crate sets an explicit `readme`, so Cargo uses the default `README.md`. Before opening a PR, for every crate the work touches check whether the change affects that crate's public API / usage example, its install or feature story, or its published status (a stub ascending to published, a renamed/added feature flag); if so, bring its `crates/<crate>/README.md` into line on the same branch — and also the facade `crates/paigasus-helikon/README.md` and the root `README.md` whenever the crate roster or the feature → module map changes. README install snippets deliberately use drift-free `cargo add` (no hardcoded versions), so a routine version bump alone needs no README edit. Like the mdBook, the READMEs drift silently otherwise — they sat as untouched 3-line SMA-304 stubs (`Stub — see SMA-304`) through all of Stage 1 while ten crates shipped real implementations; SMA-424 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no README edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip.
- Commit prefix: `<type>(<scope>): SMA-### <message>` (e.g. `feat(facade): SMA-304 ...`).
- **PR titles must satisfy two independent rules from `pr-title.yml`** (`amannn/action-semantic-pull-request`):
  1. **Full Conventional Commits format.** The action enforces a valid `type(scope):` prefix from the action's configured `types` list — independent of the subject regex. `SMA-317 add anthropic provider` (no prefix) fails; `feat(providers-anthropic): SMA-317 add anthropic provider` passes.
  2. **Subject must start lowercase after the `SMA-###` prefix.** The `subjectPattern: ^([A-Z]{2,4}-\d+ )?[^A-Z].+$` rejects `feat(core): SMA-314 LlmAgent + ...` because `L` is uppercase; lead the subject with a lowercase verb (`add`, `wire`, `pin`, `promote`, `implement`, `fix`).
  Per-commit Conventional Commit titles on the feature branch don't trip either rule — only the PR title (which becomes the squashed `main` commit) is gated.
- Linear auto-closes the linked SMA-* issue when its PR merges; no manual status move needed.
- **Always implement GitHub Actions against the latest stable major**, pinned to a commit SHA (never a moving `@vN` tag), keeping the human-readable version as a trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment **on the `uses:` line**, so the SHA is auditable. The comment must end with the version: Dependabot updates only a same-line comment that ends with the old version, so a version on its own line above the step goes stale on every bump (SMA-744). This rule applies only to pins of a tagged release. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is pinned to an untagged `master` commit, so it has no version comment. Do not add one, because no tag gives a correct version. The `gh-actions` Dependabot group sets no `update-types`, so its configuration permits major bumps in the same grouped PR. Do not depend on that: `actions/checkout` still sat on v6.0.2 until SMA-486 bumped it by hand, so **check for a new major by hand**. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is a special case: it ships rolling branches and a periodically re-pointed `v1` tag, so confirm the direction (`ahead_by > 0, behind_by == 0`) before accepting any bump — the naive "bump to latest release" recipe once would have proposed an ~11-month downgrade. Independently and permanently: every site pinning it **must** pair the SHA with an explicit `with: toolchain: …`, because a SHA ref carries no toolchain selector. Recipes and history: `docs/runbooks/github-actions-pinning.md`.
- **After a PR merges to `main`, release-plz opens/updates a `chore: release` PR** (authored by the paigasusbot App) carrying the version bumps + CHANGELOG; in the normal flow **merging that PR is what publishes to crates.io** (the merged feature PR left versions matching the registry, so its own `main` push publishes nothing). The exception is a PR that bumps its own version — the stub-ascend ritual — which publishes on its own merge with no separate release PR. Check the release PR after every merge and watch its CI — its release-PR `cargo update` can pull a fresh advisory that reddens `audit`/`deny` on the bot PR **only** (independent of `main`); fix with a `chore(deps)` pin and release-plz regenerates the PR clean.

## CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs nine jobs on every PR (`commits` is PR-only; the other eight also run on push to `main`): `fmt`, `clippy`, `test` (matrix `{ubuntu, macos, windows} × {stable, 1.94}`, `fail-fast: false`), `build-no-default-features`, `docs` (`RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`), `doc-coverage` (gated at `DOC_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD`, default 80%), `commits` (`convco check`), `sessions-it` (Postgres/Redis, path-filtered), and `markdown-lint`. The `paigasus-helikon-cli` crate is excluded from both the `missing_docs` lint and the coverage aggregator until its public API stabilizes.

`.github/workflows/integration.yml` runs `temporal-it` and `agentcore-image` as **signal-only** jobs, deliberately outside `ci.yml` so an expected flake cannot make "ci is red on `main`" meaningless. **Signal-only means *not listed as required*, never `continue-on-error`.**

`.github/workflows/msrv.yml` runs `cargo msrv --path crates/paigasus-helikon-core verify` as a non-required signal that the declared MSRV is truthful.

Supply-chain workflows (`audit.yml`, `deny.yml`, `sbom.yml`) are separate from `ci.yml` because they have independent triggers and failure semantics. `audit.yml` and `deny.yml` both run on push to `main`, PRs, a daily cron, and `workflow_dispatch`, so `main` is re-evaluated daily at exactly PR severity.

**To read an audit verdict, use the Checks API, not the legacy commit-status API** — the latter returns only `CodeRabbit` on this repo, rendering a confident `state: success` that contains no audit verdict whatsoever:

```bash
gh api repos/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/commits/main/check-runs \
  --jq '.check_runs[] | select(.name=="audit" or .name=="deny") | {name, status, conclusion}'
```

Note also that the `scheduled-audit` job's green status means nothing at any severity — read the *run* conclusion, never that job's status.

The `CARGO_*`/`RUST*`-prefixed workflow env that `rust-cache` hashes into its key must stay byte-identical across every cache-bearing workflow, enforced by `scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync.sh` running as a step in `fmt`. `audit` and `deny` deliberately cache no `target/` directory — neither compiles the workspace, so it was pure waste against the fixed budget.  CI also sets **`CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: line-tables-only`** (SMA-618 PR 2), which measured a **16.5% cut in total cache bytes** — 14-29% on the `test` legs and exactly 0% on `clippy`/`docs`/`doc-coverage`, which are metadata-mode builds with no debug info to remove. (A local sample of the largest `.rlib` files suggested 79%; do not extrapolate an aggregate from its densest component.) Keeping line tables preserves file:line in panic backtraces. Like `CARGO_TERM_COLOR`, it is **inside** rust-cache's key, so it must be byte-identical in every cache-bearing workflow — adding it to one and not the rest silently splits the cache rather than failing. `prefix-key: v1` marks the post-PR-2 generation, so any surviving `v0-` entry is provably stale and safe to purge — note it **replaces** the default `v0-rust` entirely, so keys read `v1-<job>-...`, not `v1-rust-<job>-...`. `clippy` and `docs` share one entry via `shared-key: metadata`, with `clippy` the sole writer and `docs` carrying a literal `save-if: false`; exactly one site may save a shared key, and the guard enforces it. Full rationale: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md` → "Actions cache budget".

The **`microvm`/forkd live-KVM path is not validated locally or in GitHub CI** — the dev host is arm64 macOS (no `/dev/kvm`) and GitHub runners have none. Validate it on a **GCP nested-virtualization VM** (Ubuntu 24.04 — the forkd binaries need glibc ≥ 2.38; Intel `n2`) per `docs/runbooks/forkd-live-validation.md`. The `tests/forkd_live.rs` tests are env-gated (`FORKD_URL` / `FORKD_TOKEN` / `FORKD_SNAPSHOT`) and loud-skip when no controller is configured, so `cargo test` stays green without one.

## Local hooks

Hooks are managed via `cargo-husky` (user-hooks mode) and live in `.cargo-husky/hooks/`. They install into `.git/hooks/` on the next dev-dep realization of `paigasus-helikon`. To force a re-install after editing one: `rm -rf target/debug/build/cargo-husky-* && cargo test -p paigasus-helikon --no-run`.

- **`commit-msg`** — runs `convco check --from-stdin` (enforces the `.versionrc` allowlist).
- **`pre-commit`** — intentional no-op (`exit 0`). The file exists to claim the slot so future cargo-husky upgrades don't fill it in with surprise behavior.
- **`pre-push`** — runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `convco check <merge-base>..HEAD`. Catches the three fastest CI gates pre-push; deliberately omits `cargo test` and `cargo doc` (too slow for every push). Bypass for WIP branches: `git push --no-verify`.

Three rules here are easy to get wrong, and each has already cost a debugging session:

- **The re-install silently does nothing inside a git worktree** — cargo-husky searches for a `.git` *directory* and a worktree's is a file, so it installs nothing and the old hook keeps running. Run the re-install from the **main checkout**, and verify with `grep` against the installed copy rather than assuming.
- **Never hand-copy a hook onto `.git/hooks/<name>`** — on this machine the Entire CLI owns `pre-push` and chains to `.git/hooks/pre-push.pre-entire`, which is where the cargo-husky hook actually lives. Check for a `.pre-entire` sibling first and install into that slot.
- **The convco baseline must be a merge-base, not a branch tip** — `convco check A..B` silently falls back to walking the entire history when `A` is not an ancestor of `B`, rejecting correct branches with failures the author did not write.

Mechanics and the SMA-547 postmortem: `docs/runbooks/local-hooks.md`.

## Fixture line endings

`.gitattributes` pins `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/tests/fixtures/*.txt` to `text eol=lf`. The streaming tests `include_str!` the SSE fixtures and split them on literal `\n` delimiters; without this, Windows checkouts produce CRLF bytes and the literal-string splits return one part instead of two. When adding wire-format fixtures elsewhere that the test code parses byte-level, extend the rule.

Provenance headers for wire-format fixtures follow `CONTRIBUTING.md` → "Wire-format fixtures".

348	async fn assert_conforms_with(

351	    pinned_uncaptured: &[(&str, Scenario, &str, &str)],
352	) {
353	    let name = subject.name();
354	    let mut declined: Vec<(Scenario, &'static str)> = Vec::new();
355	    let mut uncaptured: Vec<(Scenario, &'static str)> = Vec::new();

357	    for &scenario in Scenario::ALL {
358	        let cancel = CancellationToken::new();
359	        let (stream, gate) = match subject.stream(scenario, cancel.clone()).await {
360	            Outcome::Declined(reason) => {
361	                declined.push((scenario, reason));
362	                continue;
363	            }
364	            Outcome::Uncaptured(reason) => {
365	                uncaptured.push((scenario, reason));
366	                continue;
367	            }
368	            Outcome::Served { stream, gate } => (stream, gate),
369	        };

372	        let expected = scenario.expects_stop_reason();
373	        if declared != expected {
374	            fail(
375	                name,
376	                scenario,
377	                &Violation::StopReasonDeclarationMismatch { expected, declared },
378	                "the subject's fixture does not encode what this scenario requires, so \
379	                 assertions 3 and 4 would be checked against the wrong condition",
380	            );
381	        }
382	
383	        let cancelled = is_cancel_scenario(scenario);
384	        if cancelled && gate.is_none() {
385	            fail(
386	                name,
387	                scenario,
388	                &Violation::InsufficientEvidence(
389	                    "a cancellation scenario was served without a gate, so the whole body was \
390	                     already on its way and cancellation could not truncate anything",
391	                ),
392	                "give the script a `gate_after` and hand the `GateHandle` back in \
393	                 `Outcome::Served`",
394	            );
395	        }
396	
397	        let Ok(drained) =
398	            tokio::time::timeout(DRAIN_TIMEOUT, drain(stream, gate, scenario, cancel)).await
399	        else {
400	            fail(
401	                name,
402	                scenario,
403	                &Violation::Timeout,
404	                "the stream never ended. For a cancellation scenario, check that the driver \
405	                 selects on the cancellation token while awaiting the next chunk; otherwise \
406	                 check that the script's ending actually closes the body",
407	            );
408	        };
409	
410	        if let Some(violation) = floor_violation(
411	            scenario,
412	            &drained.events,
413	            subject.fixture_tool_name(),
414	            subject.fixture_finish_reason(scenario),
415	            subject.fixture_channel_order(scenario),
416	        ) {
417	            fail(
418	                name,
419	                scenario,
420	                &violation,
421	                &format!("observed: {}", summarise(&drained.events)),
422	            );
423	        }
424	
425	        if let Some(violation) = drained.cancel_violation() {
426	            fail(
427	                name,
428	                scenario,
429	                &violation,
430	                &format!("observed: {}", summarise(&drained.events)),
431	            );
432	        }
433	
434	        if let Some(violation) = classify(&drained.events, scenario, cancelled) {
435	            fail(
436	                name,
437	                scenario,
438	                &violation,
439	                &format!("observed: {}", summarise(&drained.events)),
440	            );
441	        }
442	    }
443	
444	    let expected_declined: Vec<(Scenario, &str)> = pinned_declined
445	        .iter()
446	        .filter(|(n, _, _)| *n == name)
447	        .map(|(_, sc, r)| (*sc, *r))
448	        .collect();
449	    let expected_uncaptured: Vec<(Scenario, &str)> = pinned_uncaptured
450	        .iter()
451	        .filter(|(n, _, _, _)| *n == name)
452	        .map(|(_, sc, r, _)| (*sc, *r))
453	        .collect();
454	
455	    let mut problems = pinned_problems(PinnedKind::Declined, &declined, &expected_declined);
456	    problems.extend(pinned_problems(
457	        PinnedKind::Uncaptured,
458	        &uncaptured,
459	        &expected_uncaptured,
460	    ));

462	        problems.is_empty(),
463	        "conformance: {name} — the observed decline or uncaptured set does not match the \
464	         pinned DECLINED or UNCAPTURED table (spec §6.2, §6.4):\n{}",
465	        problems.join("\n")
466	    );
467	}

471	    matches!(

494	    /// `false` means the stream ended by itself first.

496	    /// The server was still parked on the gate when the stream ended, so the

504	        let evidence = self.cancel.as_ref()?;

507	                "the stream ended on its own before cancellation was fired, so this scenario \

511	        if !evidence.server_was_parked {

525	/// sent before the gate; wait for the stream to fall quiet, which is what
526	/// proves the server is withholding; fire the token; read whatever the driver

528	/// whether the server really was parked on it.
529	///
530	/// The gate is deliberately *not* released before cancelling. Releasing first
531	/// would put the rest of the script on the wire in a race with the token, so a
532	/// correct driver could emit `Finish` from an already-delivered terminator
533	/// before it ever observed the cancellation, and the suite would report
534	/// `FinishOnCancel` against provider code that did nothing wrong.
535	async fn drain(
536	    mut stream: BoxStream<'static, Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>,
537	    gate: Option<GateHandle>,
538	    scenario: Scenario,
539	    cancel: CancellationToken,
540	) -> Drained {

554	            cancel: None,

558	    let mut fired = false;
559	    loop {
560	        match tokio::time::timeout(GATE_QUIESCENCE, stream.next()).await {
561	            Ok(Some(event)) => events.push(event),
562	            // The stream ended by itself: the gate withheld nothing.
563	            Ok(None) => break,
564	            Err(_) => {
565	                // The stream has fallen silent, so the server is parked on the
566	                // gate. Fire the token while STILL HOLDING the gate. Do not
567	                // "simplify" this by releasing first: that puts the rest of the
568	                // script on the wire in a race with the token, so a correct
569	                // driver can emit `Finish` from an already-delivered terminator
570	                // before it ever observes the cancellation — and the suite would
571	                // report `FinishOnCancel` against provider code that did nothing
572	                // wrong, intermittently, depending on machine load. Holding is
573	                // also what makes the truncation provable further down.

576	                break;
577	            }
578	        }

585	    }

590	        cancel: Some(CancelEvidence {
591	            fired,
592	            server_was_parked,
593	        }),

653	            {
