# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this is

The Paigasus AI SDK (codename **Helikon**, after Mt Helicon where Pegasus's hoof struck the Hippocrene spring). A Rust SDK for building AI agents. All crates live under the `paigasus-helikon-*` namespace.

The full architectural reference lives in Notion: ["Crate Reference"](https://www.notion.so/355830e8fbaa813c92e8c1aa9985fd3f). Linear project: `Paigasus Helikon` (issues prefixed `SMA-`).

## Common commands

```bash
cargo build --workspace                              # all 14 crates
cargo build --workspace --all-features               # facade with every optional crate
cargo run -p paigasus-helikon-cli --bin helikon
cargo run -p paigasus-helikon-cli --bin paigasus-helikon
```

To reproduce **every** CI gate locally (matches `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job-for-job):

```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --all-features
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps
DOC_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD=80 NIGHTLY_CHANNEL=nightly-2026-05-01 \
  bash scripts/check-doc-coverage.sh                 # requires: rustup toolchain install nightly-2026-05-01
npm ci                                               # once, or after package-lock.json changes
npx markdownlint-cli2                                # reads .markdownlint-cli2.jsonc
bash scripts/check-markdownlint-config.sh            # asserts that config is in force
bash scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync.sh         # cargo-visible workflow env is uniform
bash scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync-selftest.sh # …and its parser still parses (fmt runs both)
bash scripts/check-release-gaps-selftest.sh            # release gap report + release-plz.yml guards (fmt runs it)
bash scripts/check-breaking-cascade-selftest.sh      # the cascade guard keeps its rule (fmt runs it)
bash scripts/check-breaking-cascade.sh                 # breaking bump needs breaking dependents (PR only; fmt runs it)
```

The full list lives in `CONTRIBUTING.md` (single source of truth for contributor policies).

## Workspace layout

15 crates under `crates/`. The facade `paigasus-helikon` re-exports `paigasus-helikon-core` unconditionally and the other 12 sibling crates behind Cargo features.

Every crate carries a real implementation and publishes to crates.io; zero name-claim stubs remain (first published in SMA-385, last ascends in SMA-333). One standing exception: `paigasus-helikon-cli` publishes as a **binary** crate — its lib target is internal (`missing_docs` opted out), carries no stability guarantee, and exists only so `cargo install paigasus-helikon-cli` resolves. `paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit` publishes as a normal library crate (SMA-805); the three session backends keep a path-only dev-dependency on it. Exact versions move every release — read each crate's `Cargo.toml`, don't trust numbers written here.

Workspace inheritance is **mandatory**: per-crate `Cargo.toml`s only set `name`, `description`, and any crate-specific bits. Everything else (`edition`, `rust-version`, `authors`, `license`, `repository`, `homepage`, `keywords`, `categories`) inherits from `[workspace.package]` in the root `Cargo.toml`. Don't hardcode these per-crate.

**Per-crate version is the one exception.** No stubs remain, so the 4-step ascend recipe is now historical — but two caveats still bite any PR that hand-bumps a version:

- **If a crate uses `paigasus-helikon-core` API added in the *same* PR, bump `core` too**, along with its `[workspace.dependencies]` pin and CHANGELOG. `cargo publish --verify` builds the tarball against the **registry** core, so otherwise the publish fails and release-plz deadlocks.
- **Any PR that hand-bumps a sibling must ALSO bump the facade** (`crates/paigasus-helikon/Cargo.toml` version + its self-pin + CHANGELOG). release-plz does not bump the facade for a sibling version that is already at target when the PR merges, so a manual bump silently leaves the facade advertising stale dep reqs. (`dependencies_update = true` only makes the release PR run `cargo update` on `Cargo.lock`; it does not cascade version bumps.)
- **A breaking bump of a crate needs a breaking bump of each crate that depends on it.** release-plz gives a dependent without its own commits only a patch bump (release-plz#1599), and users then get two copies of the crate. The `fmt` job runs `scripts/check-breaking-cascade.sh` to enforce this. See `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md` → "A breaking change in a crate with dependents".
- Feature branches must match the `branch-names` ruleset (`feature/**` or `hotfix/**`); a `chore/**` branch is rejected at push with `GH013 … creations being restricted`.

Full lifecycle, the 4-step recipe, and the SMA-321/SMA-346 postmortems: `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md`.

Third-party version pins live in `[workspace.dependencies]` (root). Members reference them via `dep.workspace = true`. Internal crate paths are also in `[workspace.dependencies]` so the facade can use `workspace = true` consistently.

## Non-obvious patterns to preserve

- **Feature naming**: kebab-case in `[features]` (`runtime-tokio`), snake-case in `pub use` aliases (`runtime_tokio`). They must stay paired across the facade's `Cargo.toml` and `src/lib.rs`.
- **`paigasus-helikon-cli` uses `autobins = false`** because the `paigasus-helikon` (hyphen) binary maps to `src/bin/paigasus_helikon.rs` (underscore — hyphens are illegal in Rust filenames). Removing `autobins = false` reintroduces a phantom `paigasus_helikon` binary that conflicts with the explicit `[[bin]]` entry.
- **`paigasus-helikon-macros` is a proc-macro crate from day one** (`[lib] proc-macro = true`). Don't convert it to a regular lib even though it currently has no macros.
- **The `paigasus-helikon` facade lib shares its name with the `paigasus-helikon` CLI binary by design** (Notion ref's "fully-qualified shim alias"). This produces a non-fatal `cargo doc` filename-collision warning. Don't "fix" it by renaming either — both names are user-facing API. The accepted future fix is `doc = false` on the CLI binary entry.
- **License is dual `Apache-2.0 OR MIT`** (decided 2026-05-20, reversing the 2026-05-16 MIT-only call). Both `LICENSE-APACHE` and `LICENSE-MIT` live at the repo root; the workspace metadata is `license = "Apache-2.0 OR MIT"`. Per Rust ecosystem convention — no Apache-only or MIT-only crates in the workspace. Contributions are accepted under the same dual license by default (the standard inbound-equals-outbound clause is restated in `README.md`).
- **MSRV is `1.94`** (workspace-package level; raised from 1.85 in SMA-329 because sqlx 0.9.0 declares `rust-version = "1.94.0"` — the pre-existing highest floor in the workspace). If a dep raises MSRV, bump `rust-version` to what cargo demands rather than downgrading the dep.
- **Workspace-wide `missing_docs` enforcement** lives in root `Cargo.toml` (`[workspace.lints.rust] missing_docs = "warn"`). Each non-CLI crate opts in with `[lints] workspace = true`. The CLI overrides locally with `[lints.rust] missing_docs = "allow"` and does **not** include `workspace = true` — cargo treats `[lints] workspace = true` and an inline `[lints.<tool>]` table as mutually exclusive. When adding a new crate, copy the opt-in block. When adding a new `pub use` re-export to the facade, give it a `///` doc comment or `-D warnings` will fail the docs job.
- **`cargo msrv` has no `--workspace` flag.** The msrv workflow verifies one representative inheriting crate: `cargo msrv --path crates/paigasus-helikon-core verify`. Because every member uses `rust-version.workspace = true`, success on one is success on all. Don't "fix" the workflow by adding `--workspace`; that's what the first SMA-305 CI run died on.
- **Nightly is date-pinned** (`NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN: nightly-2026-05-01` at the workflow `env:` level in `ci.yml`, threaded into the doc-coverage script as `NIGHTLY_CHANNEL`). The rustdoc JSON coverage format is `-Z unstable-options` and can shift between nightlies; floating `nightly` would be a CI footgun. Bumping is a one-line follow-up chore, not an emergency.
- **Bootstrap commits on release infrastructure must use `chore(...)` or `docs(...)` types**, never `feat`/`fix`. release-plz parses every commit since the last per-crate tag — a `feat(workspace): ...` commit that touches every `Cargo.toml` would attribute a bump to every crate. The SMA-307 bootstrap PR followed this rule; the same rule applies to any future `release-plz.toml` or `release-plz.yml` edits.

## Model routing

The general tiering rules are in the global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Only the repo-specific rules are here.

- **Use Opus for release work.** This covers release-plz, the stub-ascend recipe, a hand-bumped crate version, and any red required gate. A wrong answer breaks a publish; see `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md`.
- **Haiku can read CI output.** Change to Opus when the question becomes *why* a required gate is red.

## Workflow conventions

- Branch per Linear issue: `feature/<sma-####>-<kebab-title>`. The branch name is pre-computed in each Linear ticket's `gitBranchName` field.
- Design artifacts per ticket (`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md`) land on the feature branch alongside the implementation — not pre-merged to `main`.
- **Keep the public mdBook (`docs/book/`) current — update it in the same PR as any user-facing change.** Before opening a PR, check whether the work changes public API, the quickstart/example flow, the crate roster (incl. a stub crate ascending to published), or a documented concept; if so, bring the affected `docs/book/src/*.md` page(s) into line on the same branch. The book is published from `main` and drifts silently otherwise — it sat as the untouched SMA-311 scaffold (13/17 pages still `> **Stub.**`) through all of Stage 1 before anyone noticed; SMA-423 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no book edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip. `mdbook build docs/book` must stay clean (`[output.linkcheck] warning-policy = "error"`).
- **Keep crate `README.md` files current — update the affected crate's README in the same PR as any change to its public surface.** Each of the ten published crates' `README.md` is its crates.io (and docs.rs landing-sidebar) page — no crate sets an explicit `readme`, so Cargo uses the default `README.md`. Before opening a PR, for every crate the work touches check whether the change affects that crate's public API / usage example, its install or feature story, or its published status (a stub ascending to published, a renamed/added feature flag); if so, bring its `crates/<crate>/README.md` into line on the same branch — and also the facade `crates/paigasus-helikon/README.md` and the root `README.md` whenever the crate roster or the feature → module map changes. README install snippets deliberately use drift-free `cargo add` (no hardcoded versions), so a routine version bump alone needs no README edit. Like the mdBook, the READMEs drift silently otherwise — they sat as untouched 3-line SMA-304 stubs (`Stub — see SMA-304`) through all of Stage 1 while ten crates shipped real implementations; SMA-424 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no README edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip.
- Commit prefix: `<type>(<scope>): SMA-### <message>` (e.g. `feat(facade): SMA-304 ...`).
- **PR titles must satisfy two independent rules from `pr-title.yml`** (`amannn/action-semantic-pull-request`):
  1. **Full Conventional Commits format.** The action enforces a valid `type(scope):` prefix from the action's configured `types` list — independent of the subject regex. `SMA-317 add anthropic provider` (no prefix) fails; `feat(providers-anthropic): SMA-317 add anthropic provider` passes.
  2. **Subject must start lowercase after the `SMA-###` prefix.** The `subjectPattern: ^([A-Z]{2,4}-\d+ )?[^A-Z].+$` rejects `feat(core): SMA-314 LlmAgent + ...` because `L` is uppercase; lead the subject with a lowercase verb (`add`, `wire`, `pin`, `promote`, `implement`, `fix`).
  Per-commit Conventional Commit titles on the feature branch don't trip either rule — only the PR title (which becomes the squashed `main` commit) is gated.
- Linear auto-closes the linked SMA-* issue when its PR merges; no manual status move needed.
- **Always implement GitHub Actions against the latest stable major**, pinned to a commit SHA (never a moving `@vN` tag), keeping the human-readable version as a trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment **on the `uses:` line**, so the SHA is auditable. The comment must end with the version: Dependabot updates only a same-line comment that ends with the old version, so a version on its own line above the step goes stale on every bump (SMA-744). This rule applies only to pins of a tagged release. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is pinned to an untagged `master` commit, so it has no version comment. Do not add one, because no tag gives a correct version. The `gh-actions` Dependabot group sets no `update-types`, so its configuration permits major bumps in the same grouped PR. Do not depend on that: `actions/checkout` still sat on v6.0.2 until SMA-486 bumped it by hand, so **check for a new major by hand**. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is a special case: it ships rolling branches and a periodically re-pointed `v1` tag, so confirm the direction (`ahead_by > 0, behind_by == 0`) before accepting any bump — the naive "bump to latest release" recipe once would have proposed an ~11-month downgrade. Independently and permanently: every site pinning it **must** pair the SHA with an explicit `with: toolchain: …`, because a SHA ref carries no toolchain selector. Recipes and history: `docs/runbooks/github-actions-pinning.md`.
- **After a PR merges to `main`, release-plz opens/updates a `chore: release` PR** (authored by the paigasusbot App) carrying the version bumps + CHANGELOG; in the normal flow **merging that PR is what publishes to crates.io** (the merged feature PR left versions matching the registry, so its own `main` push publishes nothing). The exception is a PR that bumps its own version — the stub-ascend ritual — which publishes on its own merge with no separate release PR. Check the release PR after every merge and watch its CI — its release-PR `cargo update` can pull a fresh advisory that reddens `audit`/`deny` on the bot PR **only** (independent of `main`); fix with a `chore(deps)` pin and release-plz regenerates the PR clean.

## CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs nine jobs on every PR (`commits` is PR-only; the other eight also run on push to `main`): `fmt`, `clippy`, `test` (matrix `{ubuntu, macos, windows} × {stable, 1.94}`, `fail-fast: false`), `build-no-default-features`, `docs` (`RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`), `doc-coverage` (gated at `DOC_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD`, default 80%), `commits` (`convco check`), `sessions-it` (Postgres/Redis, path-filtered), and `markdown-lint`. The `paigasus-helikon-cli` crate is excluded from both the `missing_docs` lint and the coverage aggregator until its public API stabilizes.

`.github/workflows/integration.yml` runs `temporal-it` and `agentcore-image` as **signal-only** jobs, deliberately outside `ci.yml` so an expected flake cannot make "ci is red on `main`" meaningless. **Signal-only means *not listed as required*, never `continue-on-error`.**

`.github/workflows/msrv.yml` runs `cargo msrv --path crates/paigasus-helikon-core verify` as a non-required signal that the declared MSRV is truthful.

Supply-chain workflows (`audit.yml`, `deny.yml`, `sbom.yml`) are separate from `ci.yml` because they have independent triggers and failure semantics. `audit.yml` and `deny.yml` both run on push to `main`, PRs, a daily cron, and `workflow_dispatch`, so `main` is re-evaluated daily at exactly PR severity.

**To read an audit verdict, use the Checks API, not the legacy commit-status API** — the latter returns only `CodeRabbit` on this repo, rendering a confident `state: success` that contains no audit verdict whatsoever:

```bash
gh api repos/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/commits/main/check-runs \
  --jq '.check_runs[] | select(.name=="audit" or .name=="deny") | {name, status, conclusion}'
```

Note also that the `scheduled-audit` job's green status means nothing at any severity — read the *run* conclusion, never that job's status.

The required-status-check contexts gated on `main` are (bare job names, as posted by the GitHub Actions app): `fmt`, `clippy`, `test (ubuntu-latest, stable)`, `test (macos-latest, stable)`, `test (windows-latest, stable)`, `docs`, `doc-coverage`, `book-build`, `commits`, `pr-title`, `audit`, `deny`, `sessions-it`, `build-no-default-features`, `markdown-lint`. The macOS job is required because it is the only gate that compiles and runs the Seatbelt backend; the Windows job because it is the only gate that exercises the Windows timeout path in `paigasus-helikon-tools` — `cmd /C` process spawning and a `TerminateProcess`-based kill, which unlike the unix path has no process-group semantics and assigns a real exit code (SMA-569); `sessions-it` because it is the only gate that runs the live Postgres/Redis session backends; `build-no-default-features` because it is the only gate that compiles `runtime-axum` and `runtime-actix` with default features off. The canonical declaration is `.github/rulesets/main-protection-checks.json` (see CONTRIBUTING.md → "Repo configuration"). Other matrix variants (the `1.94` legs) run as signals only.

These pins are hand-bumped with nothing tracking them: `TEMPORAL_CLI_VERSION`/`TEMPORAL_CLI_SHA256` in `integration.yml`, `NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN` in `ci.yml`, `convco@…` in `ci.yml`'s `commits` job, `MDBOOK_VERSION`/`MDBOOK_LINKCHECK_VERSION` in `docs.yml`, and `markdownlint-cli2` via `package-lock.json`. **A checksum mismatch is never a signal to update the digest** — the causes are, in order, a truncated download, an upstream re-tag, and tampering; verify upstream independently first.

**The workspace needs no system `protoc`** (SMA-623): `temporalio-client`'s `vendored-protox` feature compiles the Temporal protos with `protox`. `ci.yml` sets `PROTOC` to a path that does not exist, and `build-no-default-features` asserts that the feature is active. If a build fails with "Could not find `protoc`", do not add a `protoc` install — find which build script calls it. Rationale and recovery: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md` → "protoc and protox".

Job-by-job rationale, the audit/deny signal semantics, and the incident history behind all of the above: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md`.

**GitHub's 10 GB Actions cache limit is a standing constraint, not a one-time cleanup** (SMA-618): it is GitHub's **default**, not a hard ceiling — a repo admin, org owner or enterprise owner can raise it (user-owned repos up to 10 TB) at additional storage cost, and SMA-618 deliberately chose to fit inside it rather than pay. Enforced at 10 **GiB** (10,737,418,240 bytes) despite the "10 GB" wording. Going over fails nothing — it just triggers silent LRU eviction that makes CI legs run cold at random. `cache-budget.yml` monitors it daily and warns (never fails) above 8.5 GiB. Caches are saved **only** from `main` (`save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}` on every `Swatinem/rust-cache` site) so a PR job can still restore an entry `main` wrote but never writes a competing `refs/pull/N/merge` entry that evicts it. The `CARGO_*`/`RUST*`-prefixed workflow env that `rust-cache` hashes into its key must stay byte-identical across every cache-bearing workflow, enforced by `scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync.sh` running as a step in `fmt`. `audit` and `deny` deliberately cache no `target/` directory — neither compiles the workspace, so it was pure waste against the fixed budget.  CI also sets **`CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: line-tables-only`** (SMA-618 PR 2), which measured a **16.5% cut in total cache bytes** — 14-29% on the `test` legs and exactly 0% on `clippy`/`docs`/`doc-coverage`, which are metadata-mode builds with no debug info to remove. (A local sample of the largest `.rlib` files suggested 79%; do not extrapolate an aggregate from its densest component.) Keeping line tables preserves file:line in panic backtraces. Like `CARGO_TERM_COLOR`, it is **inside** rust-cache's key, so it must be byte-identical in every cache-bearing workflow — adding it to one and not the rest silently splits the cache rather than failing. `prefix-key: v1` marks the post-PR-2 generation, so any surviving `v0-` entry is provably stale and safe to purge — note it **replaces** the default `v0-rust` entirely, so keys read `v1-<job>-...`, not `v1-rust-<job>-...`. `clippy` and `docs` share one entry via `shared-key: metadata`, with `clippy` the sole writer and `docs` carrying a literal `save-if: false`; exactly one site may save a shared key, and the guard enforces it. Full rationale: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md` → "Actions cache budget".

The **`microvm`/forkd live-KVM path is not validated locally or in GitHub CI** — the dev host is arm64 macOS (no `/dev/kvm`) and GitHub runners have none. Validate it on a **GCP nested-virtualization VM** (Ubuntu 24.04 — the forkd binaries need glibc ≥ 2.38; Intel `n2`) per `docs/runbooks/forkd-live-validation.md`. The `tests/forkd_live.rs` tests are env-gated (`FORKD_URL` / `FORKD_TOKEN` / `FORKD_SNAPSHOT`) and loud-skip when no controller is configured, so `cargo test` stays green without one.

## Local hooks

Hooks are managed via `cargo-husky` (user-hooks mode) and live in `.cargo-husky/hooks/`. They install into `.git/hooks/` on the next dev-dep realization of `paigasus-helikon`. To force a re-install after editing one: `rm -rf target/debug/build/cargo-husky-* && cargo test -p paigasus-helikon --no-run`.

- **`commit-msg`** — runs `convco check --from-stdin` (enforces the `.versionrc` allowlist).
- **`pre-commit`** — intentional no-op (`exit 0`). The file exists to claim the slot so future cargo-husky upgrades don't fill it in with surprise behavior.
- **`pre-push`** — runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `convco check <merge-base>..HEAD`. Catches the three fastest CI gates pre-push; deliberately omits `cargo test` and `cargo doc` (too slow for every push). Bypass for WIP branches: `git push --no-verify`.

Three rules here are easy to get wrong, and each has already cost a debugging session:

- **The re-install silently does nothing inside a git worktree** — cargo-husky searches for a `.git` *directory* and a worktree's is a file, so it installs nothing and the old hook keeps running. Run the re-install from the **main checkout**, and verify with `grep` against the installed copy rather than assuming.
- **Never hand-copy a hook onto `.git/hooks/<name>`** — on this machine the Entire CLI owns `pre-push` and chains to `.git/hooks/pre-push.pre-entire`, which is where the cargo-husky hook actually lives. Check for a `.pre-entire` sibling first and install into that slot.
- **The convco baseline must be a merge-base, not a branch tip** — `convco check A..B` silently falls back to walking the entire history when `A` is not an ancestor of `B`, rejecting correct branches with failures the author did not write.

Mechanics and the SMA-547 postmortem: `docs/runbooks/local-hooks.md`.

## Fixture line endings

`.gitattributes` pins `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/tests/fixtures/*.txt` to `text eol=lf`. The streaming tests `include_str!` the SSE fixtures and split them on literal `\n` delimiters; without this, Windows checkouts produce CRLF bytes and the literal-string splits return one part instead of two. When adding wire-format fixtures elsewhere that the test code parses byte-level, extend the rule.

Provenance headers for wire-format fixtures follow `CONTRIBUTING.md` → "Wire-format fixtures".

989	    /// break at compile time the moment a variant is added, but `ALL` itself
990	    /// is just an array literal — a variant added there and nowhere else
991	    /// would compile clean and simply never run in `assert_conforms`, with
992	    /// every subject staying green.
993	    ///
994	    /// The `match` below is exhaustive over the `Scenario` *type*, so it
995	    /// fails to compile as soon as the enum grows a variant not named in
996	    /// this list, independent of what this list or `ALL` contains at
997	    /// runtime. That forces every variant to be named here, and each one is
998	    /// then checked directly against `ALL`, so a variant the type has but
999	    /// `ALL` is missing — freshly added, or dropped by accident — fails this
1000	    /// test instead of silently never running.
1001	    #[test]
1002	    fn scenario_all_is_exhaustive() {
1003	        for variant in [
1004	            Scenario::CleanStop,
1005	            Scenario::TruncatedAfterStopReason,
1006	            Scenario::TruncatedMidGeneration,
1007	            Scenario::ErrorMidGeneration,
1008	            Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason,
1009	            Scenario::CancelMidGeneration,
1010	            Scenario::CancelAfterStopReason,
1011	            Scenario::FragmentedToolName,
1012	            Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop,
1013	            Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop,
1014	            Scenario::ReasoningCleanStop,
1015	        ] {
1016	            match variant {
1017	                Scenario::CleanStop
1018	                | Scenario::TruncatedAfterStopReason
1019	                | Scenario::TruncatedMidGeneration
1020	                | Scenario::ErrorMidGeneration
1021	                | Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason
1022	                | Scenario::CancelMidGeneration
1023	                | Scenario::CancelAfterStopReason
1024	                | Scenario::FragmentedToolName
1025	                | Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop
1026	                | Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop
1027	                | Scenario::ReasoningCleanStop => assert!(
1028	                    Scenario::ALL.contains(&variant),
1029	                    "{variant:?} is missing from Scenario::ALL"
1030	                ),
1031	            }
1032	        }
1033	    }

1041	        /// script. The only correct state.

1043	        /// The server ran its script to the end without ever pausing, so the

1173	    /// A stream of `events`, optionally staying open afterwards.
1174	    fn stream_of(
1175	        events: Vec<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>,
1176	        open_until: Option<CancellationToken>,
1177	        forever: bool,
1178	    ) -> BoxStream<'static, Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>> {
1179	        let head = futures_util::stream::iter(events);
1180	        if forever {
1181	            return head.chain(futures_util::stream::pending()).boxed();
1182	        }
1183	        match open_until {
1184	            None => head.boxed(),
1185	            Some(cancel) => head
1186	                .chain(
1187	                    futures_util::stream::once(async move { cancel.cancelled().await })
1188	                        .filter_map(|()| std::future::ready(None)),
1189	                )
1190	                .boxed(),
1191	        }
1192	    }

1209	        /// scenarios, `Stop` for the other two that end with a `Finish`.
1210	        fn fixture_finish_reason(&self, scenario: Scenario) -> Option<FinishReason> {
1211	            match scenario {
1212	                Scenario::CleanStop => match self.finish_reason {
1213	                    FinishDecl::WrongOnCleanStop => Some(FinishReason::ToolCalls),
1214	                    FinishDecl::Absent => None,
1215	                    _ => Some(FinishReason::Stop),
1216	                },
1217	                Scenario::TruncatedAfterStopReason => match self.finish_reason {
1218	                    FinishDecl::WrongOnTruncation => Some(FinishReason::ToolCalls),
1219	                    _ => Some(FinishReason::Stop),
1220	                },
1221	                Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop
1222	                | Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop

1228	        fn fixture_channel_order(&self, scenario: Scenario) -> Option<&'static [Channel]> {
1229	            (scenario == Scenario::ReasoningCleanStop).then_some(&[

1234	                as &'static [Channel])

1237	        async fn stream(&self, scenario: Scenario, cancel: CancellationToken) -> Outcome {
1238	            if let Some((_, reason)) = self.declines.iter().find(|(s, _)| *s == scenario) {
1239	                return Outcome::Declined(reason);
1240	            }
1241	            if let Some((_, reason)) = self.uncaptured.iter().find(|(s, _)| *s == scenario) {
1242	                return Outcome::Uncaptured(reason);
1243	            }
1244	
1245	            let events = self.events(scenario);
1246	            let stalls = self.stalls_on == Some(scenario);
1247	
1248	            if !is_cancel_scenario(scenario) {
1249	                return Outcome::Served {
1250	                    stream: stream_of(events, None, stalls),
1251	                    gate: None,
1252	                };
1253	            }
1254	
1255	            let open_until = self.holds_open.then_some(cancel);
1256	            let stream = stream_of(events, open_until, stalls);
1257	            let gate = match self.gate {
1258	                Gate::Absent => None,
1259	                Gate::Parked => {
1260	                    let (tx, rx) = oneshot::channel();
1261	                    self.held
1262	                        .lock()
1263	                        .expect("gate-receiver mutex should not be poisoned")
1264	                        .push(rx);
1265	                    Some(GateHandle { tx })
1266	                }
1267	                Gate::Finished => {
1268	                    let (tx, _rx) = oneshot::channel();
1269	                    Some(GateHandle { tx })
1270	                }
1271	            };
1272	            Outcome::Served { stream, gate }
1273	        }
1274	    }

1	//! Fake model streams that prove the checker can fail.
     2	//!
     3	//! Each non-conforming variant violates exactly one rule, and the tests below
     4	//! assert that [`classify`] rejects it with the classification the design spec
     5	//! names for that rule (§8). This runs on every CI run, so the suite cannot
     6	//! silently decay into one that always passes.
     7	//!
     8	//! These fakes exercise the **checker**, not the HTTP path: `run` builds the
     9	//! event vector in memory and classifies it, so no server, no transport and no
    10	//! provider crate is involved. The floors and the decline cross-check in
    11	//! `assert_conforms` are therefore not on this path — a fake can never be
    12	//! rejected by a floor instead of by the classification it is written to
    13	//! trigger.
    14	
    15	use crate::{classify, Scenario, Violation};
    16	use paigasus_helikon_core::{FinishReason, ModelError, ModelEvent};
    17	
    18	/// The tool name every tool-bearing fake declares.
    19	pub(crate) const TOOL_NAME: &str = "get_weather";
    20	
    21	/// The `call_id` every tool-bearing fake uses. The tests pin the reported
    22	/// violation against this exact string, so it is shared rather than repeated.
    23	const CALL_ID: &str = "c1";
    24	
    25	/// A stream shape that violates exactly one rule — plus [`Fake::Conforming`],
    26	/// which violates none.
    27	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
    28	pub enum Fake {
    29	    /// A `TokenDelta` after `Finish` (assertion 1).
    30	    EventAfterFinish,
    31	    /// An `Err` after `Finish` (assertion 1).
    32	    ErrAfterFinish,
    33	    /// Two `Finish` events (assertion 1).
    34	    DoubleFinish,
    35	    /// A `Usage` after `Finish` — the SMA-522 shape (assertion 2).
    36	    UsageAfterFinish,
    37	    /// End-of-stream after an observed stop reason with no `Finish` — the
    38	    /// SMA-531 shape (assertion 3).
    39	    NoFinishAfterStopReason,
    40	    /// A `Finish` although no stop reason was observed (assertion 4).
    41	    FinishOnTruncation,
    42	    /// A `Finish` after cancellation (assertion 5).
    43	    FinishOnCancel,
    44	    /// A `Finish` after a mid-stream error (assertion 6).
    45	    FinishAfterError,
    46	    /// A `TokenDelta` after an `Err` (assertion 9).
    47	    TokenAfterError,
    48	    /// A call-scoped `ProviderData` for a `call_id` no tool call streamed
    49	    /// (assertion 8).
    50	    ProviderDataUnknownCall,
    51	    /// Two name-bearing deltas for one `call_id` — the SMA-550 shape
    52	    /// (assertion 7).
    53	    TwoNamedDeltas,
    54	    /// Tool-call deltas that never carry a name, which is what the "exactly
    55	    /// one" tightening of assertion 7 exists to catch.
    56	    NoNamedDelta,
    57	    /// Truncated tool arguments on a stream that finishes (assertion 10).
    58	    ArgsNotJson,
    59	    /// A sequence that satisfies every assertion for the given scenario.
    60	    Conforming,
    61	}
    62	
    63	impl Fake {
    64	    /// Build this fake's event sequence for `scenario` and classify it.
    65	    ///
    66	    /// `cancelled` is derived from the scenario rather than passed in, so a
    67	    /// fake can never be tested under a cancellation flag that contradicts the
    68	    /// script it is emitting.
    69	    pub async fn run(self, scenario: Scenario) -> Option<Violation> {
    70	        classify(
    71	            &self.events(scenario),
    72	            scenario,
    73	            crate::is_cancel_scenario(scenario),
    74	        )
    75	    }
    76	
    77	    /// The event sequence this fake emits for `scenario`.
    78	    ///
    79	    /// Every non-conforming variant is built by perturbing
    80	    /// [`Fake::Conforming`]'s sequence for the *same* scenario, so each fake
    81	    /// differs from a passing stream by exactly the one rule it violates —
    82	    /// there is no hand-written sequence that could accidentally break a
    83	    /// second rule and be rejected for the wrong reason.
    84	    fn events(self, scenario: Scenario) -> Vec<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>> {
    85	        let mut events = conforming(scenario);
    86	        match self {
    87	            Fake::Conforming => {}
    88	            Fake::EventAfterFinish => events.push(token("trailing")),
    89	            Fake::ErrAfterFinish => events.push(Err(ModelError::Unavailable)),
    90	            // The scenarios these three are tested under differ, and so does
    91	            // the rule each one breaks: appending a `Finish` to a stream that
    92	            // already has one breaks assertion 1, to a truncated one breaks
    93	            // assertion 4, to a cancelled one breaks assertion 5, and to an
    94	            // errored one breaks assertion 6.
    95	            Fake::DoubleFinish
    96	            | Fake::FinishOnTruncation
    97	            | Fake::FinishOnCancel
    98	            | Fake::FinishAfterError => events.push(finish(scenario)),
    99	            Fake::TokenAfterError => events.push(token("trailing")),
   100	            Fake::ProviderDataUnknownCall => {
   101	                // Insert before the `Finish` so assertion 1 stays satisfied.
   102	                let at = events
   103	                    .iter()
   104	                    .position(|e| matches!(e, Ok(ModelEvent::Finish { .. })))
   105	                    .expect("this fake must be run under a scenario that finishes");
   106	                events.insert(
   107	                    at,
   108	                    Ok(ModelEvent::ProviderData {
   109	                        provider: "test".into(),
   110	                        call_id: Some("x".into()),
   111	                        data: serde_json::json!({ "kind": "tool_use" }),
   112	                    }),
   113	                );
   114	            }
   115	            Fake::UsageAfterFinish => {
   116	                events.retain(|e| !matches!(e, Ok(ModelEvent::Usage { .. })));
   117	                events.push(usage());
   118	            }
   119	            Fake::NoFinishAfterStopReason => {
   120	                events.retain(|e| !matches!(e, Ok(ModelEvent::Finish { .. })));
   121	            }
   122	            Fake::TwoNamedDeltas => {
   123	                // Split the name across both deltas instead of emitting it
   124	                // once, leaving everything else about the sequence intact.
   125	                replace_tool_deltas(
   126	                    &mut events,
   127	                    &[
   128	                        (Some("get_"), "{\"city\":"),
   129	                        (Some("weather"), "\"Berlin\"}"),
   130	                    ],
   131	                );
   132	            }
   133	            Fake::ArgsNotJson => {
   134	                replace_tool_deltas(&mut events, &[(Some(TOOL_NAME), "{\"city\":")]);
   135	            }
   136	            Fake::NoNamedDelta => {
   137	                replace_tool_deltas(&mut events, &[(None, "{\"city\":\"Berlin\"}")]);
   138	            }
   139	        }
   140	        events
   141	    }
   142	}
   143	
   144	/// The sequence a conforming subject emits for `scenario`.
   145	///
   146	/// A `Usage` and a `Finish` appear only when the scenario lets the translator
   147	/// observe a stop reason *and* the stream is neither cancelled nor errored —
   148	/// withholding `Finish` is what the contract requires in those two cases.
   149	pub(crate) fn conforming(scenario: Scenario) -> Vec<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>> {
   150	    let mut events = Vec::new();
   151	    if scenario == Scenario::ReasoningCleanStop {
   152	        // One reasoning run before the text run: the order the scenario
   153	        // declares (`Reasoning`, `Text`, `Tool`).
   154	        events.push(Ok(ModelEvent::ReasoningDelta {
   155	            text: "think".into(),
   156	        }));
   157	    }
   158	    events.push(token("hi"));
   159	
   160	    if matches!(
   161	        scenario,
   162	        Scenario::FragmentedToolName
   163	            | Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop
   164	            | Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop
   165	            | Scenario::ReasoningCleanStop
   166	    ) {
   167	        events.push(tool(Some(TOOL_NAME), "{\"city\":"));
   168	        events.push(tool(None, "\"Berlin\"}"));
   169	    }
   170	    if scenario == Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop {
   171	        // The position record of the tool call, scoped to the fake call.
   172	        events.push(Ok(ModelEvent::ProviderData {
   173	            provider: "test".into(),
   174	            call_id: Some(CALL_ID.into()),
   175	            data: serde_json::json!({ "kind": "tool_use" }),
   176	        }));
   177	    }
   178	
   179	    let errored = matches!(
   180	        scenario,
   181	        Scenario::ErrorMidGeneration | Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason
   182	    );
   183	    let cancelled = matches!(
   184	        scenario,
   185	        Scenario::CancelMidGeneration | Scenario::CancelAfterStopReason
   186	    );
   187	    if scenario.expects_stop_reason() && !errored {
   188	        // `CancelAfterStopReason` gets the `Usage` but not the `Finish`. That
   189	        // is not a detail: its script places a usage chunk *after* the
   190	        // stop-reason chunk and gates on it, so a conforming subject really
   191	        // does emit one before the token fires — and the harness's floor looks
   192	        // for exactly that to tell S5b from a gate placed one chunk too early.
   193	        // Withholding `Finish` is what the contract requires of a cancelled
   194	        // stream, and of an errored one.
   195	        events.push(usage());
   196	        if !cancelled {
   197	            events.push(finish(scenario));
   198	        }
   199	    }
   200	
   201	    if matches!(
   202	        scenario,
   203	        Scenario::ErrorMidGeneration | Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason
   204	    ) {
   205	        events.push(Err(ModelError::Unavailable));
   206	    }
   207	
   208	    events
   209	}
   210	
   211	/// Swap every `ToolCallDelta` in `events` for `deltas`, in place, keeping the
   212	/// position of the first one. Used to perturb only the tool-call half of a
   213	/// conforming sequence.
   214	fn replace_tool_deltas(
   215	    events: &mut Vec<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>,
   216	    deltas: &[(Option<&str>, &str)],
   217	) {
   218	    let at = events
   219	        .iter()
   220	        .position(|e| matches!(e, Ok(ModelEvent::ToolCallDelta { .. })))
   221	        .expect("a tool-call fake must be run under a tool-call scenario");
   222	    events.retain(|e| !matches!(e, Ok(ModelEvent::ToolCallDelta { .. })));
   223	    for (offset, (name, args)) in deltas.iter().enumerate() {
   224	        events.insert(at + offset, tool(*name, args));
   225	    }
   226	}
   227	
   228	/// A text delta.
   229	fn token(text: &str) -> Result<ModelEvent, ModelError> {
   230	    Ok(ModelEvent::TokenDelta { text: text.into() })
   231	}
   232	
   233	/// A usage snapshot.
   234	fn usage() -> Result<ModelEvent, ModelError> {
   235	    Ok(ModelEvent::Usage {
   236	        input_tokens: 7,
   237	        output_tokens: 3,
   238	        cached_input_tokens: None,
   239	        reasoning_tokens: None,
   240	    })
   241	}
   242	
   243	/// The terminal event, carrying the reason the scenario's script would encode.
   244	fn finish(scenario: Scenario) -> Result<ModelEvent, ModelError> {
   245	    Ok(ModelEvent::Finish {
   246	        reason: match scenario {
   247	            Scenario::FragmentedToolName
   248	            | Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop
   249	            | Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop
   250	            | Scenario::ReasoningCleanStop => FinishReason::ToolCalls,
   251	            _ => FinishReason::Stop,
   252	        },
   253	    })
   254	}
   255	
   256	/// One tool-call delta for [`CALL_ID`].
   257	fn tool(name: Option<&str>, args_delta: &str) -> Result<ModelEvent, ModelError> {
   258	    Ok(ModelEvent::ToolCallDelta {
   259	        call_id: CALL_ID.into(),
   260	        name: name.map(str::to_owned),
   261	        args_delta: args_delta.into(),
   262	    })
   263	}

   265	#[cfg(test)]

   269

   297	                Fake::NoFinishAfterStopReason,

   301	            (
   302	                Fake::FinishOnTruncation,

   305	            ),
   306	            (

   310	            ),
   311	            (
   312	                Fake::FinishAfterError,
   313	                Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason,

   315	            ),
   316	            (
   317	                Fake::TokenAfterError,
   318	                Scenario::ErrorMidGeneration,
   319	                Violation::EventAfterError,
   320	            ),

1	//! Fake model streams that prove the checker can fail.
     2	//!
     3	//! Each non-conforming variant violates exactly one rule, and the tests below
     4	//! assert that [`classify`] rejects it with the classification the design spec
     5	//! names for that rule (§8). This runs on every CI run, so the suite cannot
     6	//! silently decay into one that always passes.
     7	//!
     8	//! These fakes exercise the **checker**, not the HTTP path: `run` builds the
     9	//! event vector in memory and classifies it, so no server, no transport and no
    10	//! provider crate is involved. The floors and the decline cross-check in
    11	//! `assert_conforms` are therefore not on this path — a fake can never be
    12	//! rejected by a floor instead of by the classification it is written to
    13	//! trigger.
    14	
    15	use crate::{classify, Scenario, Violation};
    16	use paigasus_helikon_core::{FinishReason, ModelError, ModelEvent};
    17	
    18	/// The tool name every tool-bearing fake declares.
    19	pub(crate) const TOOL_NAME: &str = "get_weather";
    20	
    21	/// The `call_id` every tool-bearing fake uses. The tests pin the reported
    22	/// violation against this exact string, so it is shared rather than repeated.
    23	const CALL_ID: &str = "c1";
    24	
    25	/// A stream shape that violates exactly one rule — plus [`Fake::Conforming`],
    26	/// which violates none.
    27	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
    28	pub enum Fake {
    29	    /// A `TokenDelta` after `Finish` (assertion 1).
    30	    EventAfterFinish,
    31	    /// An `Err` after `Finish` (assertion 1).
    32	    ErrAfterFinish,
    33	    /// Two `Finish` events (assertion 1).
    34	    DoubleFinish,
    35	    /// A `Usage` after `Finish` — the SMA-522 shape (assertion 2).
    36	    UsageAfterFinish,
    37	    /// End-of-stream after an observed stop reason with no `Finish` — the
    38	    /// SMA-531 shape (assertion 3).
    39	    NoFinishAfterStopReason,
    40	    /// A `Finish` although no stop reason was observed (assertion 4).
    41	    FinishOnTruncation,
    42	    /// A `Finish` after cancellation (assertion 5).
    43	    FinishOnCancel,
    44	    /// A `Finish` after a mid-stream error (assertion 6).
    45	    FinishAfterError,
    46	    /// A `TokenDelta` after an `Err` (assertion 9).
    47	    TokenAfterError,
    48	    /// A call-scoped `ProviderData` for a `call_id` no tool call streamed
    49	    /// (assertion 8).
    50	    ProviderDataUnknownCall,
    51	    /// Two name-bearing deltas for one `call_id` — the SMA-550 shape
    52	    /// (assertion 7).
    53	    TwoNamedDeltas,
    54	    /// Tool-call deltas that never carry a name, which is what the "exactly
    55	    /// one" tightening of assertion 7 exists to catch.
    56	    NoNamedDelta,
    57	    /// Truncated tool arguments on a stream that finishes (assertion 10).
    58	    ArgsNotJson,
    59	    /// A sequence that satisfies every assertion for the given scenario.
    60	    Conforming,
    61	}
    62	
    63	impl Fake {
    64	    /// Build this fake's event sequence for `scenario` and classify it.
    65	    ///
    66	    /// `cancelled` is derived from the scenario rather than passed in, so a
    67	    /// fake can never be tested under a cancellation flag that contradicts the
    68	    /// script it is emitting.
    69	    pub async fn run(self, scenario: Scenario) -> Option<Violation> {
    70	        classify(
    71	            &self.events(scenario),
    72	            scenario,
    73	            crate::is_cancel_scenario(scenario),
    74	        )
    75	    }
    76	
    77	    /// The event sequence this fake emits for `scenario`.
    78	    ///
    79	    /// Every non-conforming variant is built by perturbing
    80	    /// [`Fake::Conforming`]'s sequence for the *same* scenario, so each fake
    81	    /// differs from a passing stream by exactly the one rule it violates —
    82	    /// there is no hand-written sequence that could accidentally break a
    83	    /// second rule and be rejected for the wrong reason.
    84	    fn events(self, scenario: Scenario) -> Vec<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>> {
    85	        let mut events = conforming(scenario);
    86	        match self {
    87	            Fake::Conforming => {}
    88	            Fake::EventAfterFinish => events.push(token("trailing")),
    89	            Fake::ErrAfterFinish => events.push(Err(ModelError::Unavailable)),
    90	            // The scenarios these three are tested under differ, and so does
    91	            // the rule each one breaks: appending a `Finish` to a stream that
    92	            // already has one breaks assertion 1, to a truncated one breaks
    93	            // assertion 4, to a cancelled one breaks assertion 5, and to an
    94	            // errored one breaks assertion 6.
    95	            Fake::DoubleFinish
    96	            | Fake::FinishOnTruncation
    97	            | Fake::FinishOnCancel
    98	            | Fake::FinishAfterError => events.push(finish(scenario)),
    99	            Fake::TokenAfterError => events.push(token("trailing")),
   100	            Fake::ProviderDataUnknownCall => {
   101	                // Insert before the `Finish` so assertion 1 stays satisfied.
   102	                let at = events
   103	                    .iter()
   104	                    .position(|e| matches!(e, Ok(ModelEvent::Finish { .. })))
   105	                    .expect("this fake must be run under a scenario that finishes");
   106	                events.insert(
   107	                    at,
   108	                    Ok(ModelEvent::ProviderData {
   109	                        provider: "test".into(),
   110	                        call_id: Some("x".into()),
   111	                        data: serde_json::json!({ "kind": "tool_use" }),
   112	                    }),
   113	                );
   114	            }
   115	            Fake::UsageAfterFinish => {
   116	                events.retain(|e| !matches!(e, Ok(ModelEvent::Usage { .. })));
   117	                events.push(usage());
   118	            }
   119	            Fake::NoFinishAfterStopReason => {
   120	                events.retain(|e| !matches!(e, Ok(ModelEvent::Finish { .. })));
   121	            }
   122	            Fake::TwoNamedDeltas => {
   123	                // Split the name across both deltas instead of emitting it
   124	                // once, leaving everything else about the sequence intact.
   125	                replace_tool_deltas(
   126	                    &mut events,
   127	                    &[
   128	                        (Some("get_"), "{\"city\":"),
   129	                        (Some("weather"), "\"Berlin\"}"),
   130	                    ],
   131	                );
   132	            }
   133	            Fake::ArgsNotJson => {
   134	                replace_tool_deltas(&mut events, &[(Some(TOOL_NAME), "{\"city\":")]);
   135	            }
   136	            Fake::NoNamedDelta => {
   137	                replace_tool_deltas(&mut events, &[(None, "{\"city\":\"Berlin\"}")]);
   138	            }
   139	        }
   140	        events
   141	    }
   142	}
   143	
   144	/// The sequence a conforming subject emits for `scenario`.
   145	///
   146	/// A `Usage` and a `Finish` appear only when the scenario lets the translator
   147	/// observe a stop reason *and* the stream is neither cancelled nor errored —
   148	/// withholding `Finish` is what the contract requires in those two cases.
   149	pub(crate) fn conforming(scenario: Scenario) -> Vec<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>> {
   150	    let mut events = Vec::new();
   151	    if scenario == Scenario::ReasoningCleanStop {
   152	        // One reasoning run before the text run: the order the scenario
   153	        // declares (`Reasoning`, `Text`, `Tool`).
   154	        events.push(Ok(ModelEvent::ReasoningDelta {
   155	            text: "think".into(),
   156	        }));
   157	    }
   158	    events.push(token("hi"));
   159	
   160	    if matches!(
   161	        scenario,
   162	        Scenario::FragmentedToolName
   163	            | Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop
   164	            | Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop
   165	            | Scenario::ReasoningCleanStop
   166	    ) {
   167	        events.push(tool(Some(TOOL_NAME), "{\"city\":"));
   168	        events.push(tool(None, "\"Berlin\"}"));
   169	    }
   170	    if scenario == Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop {
   171	        // The position record of the tool call, scoped to the fake call.
   172	        events.push(Ok(ModelEvent::ProviderData {
   173	            provider: "test".into(),
   174	            call_id: Some(CALL_ID.into()),
   175	            data: serde_json::json!({ "kind": "tool_use" }),
   176	        }));
   177	    }
   178	
   179	    let errored = matches!(
   180	        scenario,
   181	        Scenario::ErrorMidGeneration | Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason
   182	    );
   183	    let cancelled = matches!(
   184	        scenario,
   185	        Scenario::CancelMidGeneration | Scenario::CancelAfterStopReason
   186	    );
   187	    if scenario.expects_stop_reason() && !errored {
   188	        // `CancelAfterStopReason` gets the `Usage` but not the `Finish`. That
   189	        // is not a detail: its script places a usage chunk *after* the
   190	        // stop-reason chunk and gates on it, so a conforming subject really
   191	        // does emit one before the token fires — and the harness's floor looks
   192	        // for exactly that to tell S5b from a gate placed one chunk too early.
   193	        // Withholding `Finish` is what the contract requires of a cancelled
   194	        // stream, and of an errored one.
   195	        events.push(usage());
   196	        if !cancelled {
   197	            events.push(finish(scenario));
   198	        }
   199	    }
   200	
   201	    if matches!(
   202	        scenario,
   203	        Scenario::ErrorMidGeneration | Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason
   204	    ) {
   205	        events.push(Err(ModelError::Unavailable));
   206	    }
   207	
   208	    events
   209	}
   210	
   211	/// Swap every `ToolCallDelta` in `events` for `deltas`, in place, keeping the
   212	/// position of the first one. Used to perturb only the tool-call half of a
   213	/// conforming sequence.
   214	fn replace_tool_deltas(
   215	    events: &mut Vec<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>,
   216	    deltas: &[(Option<&str>, &str)],
   217	) {
   218	    let at = events
   219	        .iter()
   220	        .position(|e| matches!(e, Ok(ModelEvent::ToolCallDelta { .. })))
   221	        .expect("a tool-call fake must be run under a tool-call scenario");
   222	    events.retain(|e| !matches!(e, Ok(ModelEvent::ToolCallDelta { .. })));
   223	    for (offset, (name, args)) in deltas.iter().enumerate() {
   224	        events.insert(at + offset, tool(*name, args));
   225	    }
   226	}
   227	
   228	/// A text delta.
   229	fn token(text: &str) -> Result<ModelEvent, ModelError> {
   230	    Ok(ModelEvent::TokenDelta { text: text.into() })
   231	}
   232	
   233	/// A usage snapshot.

81	/// `usageMetadata` despite having no `finishReason` at all, and
82	/// `multi_chunk_usage_emits_usage_per_chunk`'s first chunk (already cited

84	/// chunk, not only the terminal one. [`text_delta`] now sets `usageMetadata`

90	/// placed anywhere in this script, even before `stop_chunk`, would still show

168	        frame(json!({
169	            "candidates": [{
170	                "content": { "parts": [ { "text": text } ] }
171	            }],

174	                "candidatesTokenCount": candidates_tokens

196	            "candidates": [{
197	                "content": { "parts": [ { "text": text } ] },
198	                "finishReason": reason
199	            }],

201	                "promptTokenCount": prompt_tokens,
202	                "candidatesTokenCount": candidates_tokens
203	            }

212	    /// repo-wide grep for the literal string `[DONE]` under
213	    /// `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/` turns up only the driver's
214	    /// own comparison, never a captured or scripted SSE frame, and the live
215	    /// capture (module doc, "Live capture") itself ended at bare EOF with no

220	    /// terminator `openai_chat` and `litellm` send, since `model.rs` checks

227	    /// `thoughtSignature`, all in one `functionCall` part, plus
228	    /// `usageMetadata` — Gemini never streams a tool call incrementally, so
229	    /// this is the only shape a tool call can take on the wire (see the
230	    /// module doc's "why `FragmentedToolName` is declined" section).
231	    ///
232	    /// # Provenance
233	    ///
234	    /// Transcribed from the live capture (module doc, "Live capture"
235	    /// section) — `id`/`name`/`args`/`thoughtSignature` keys and their
236	    /// nesting match the captured bytes exactly (`thoughtSignature`'s VALUE
237	    /// is a short synthetic placeholder, not the captured blob — see
238	    /// [`THOUGHT_SIGNATURE`]). No `finishReason` key, matching the capture's
239	    /// first chunk. `sse.rs`'s `Part`/`FunctionCall` structs
240	    /// (`#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`) independently confirm the wire
241	    /// key is `functionCall` and its modelled fields are `id`/`name`/`args`.
242	    fn tool_call_chunk(
243	        call_id: &str,
244	        name: &str,
245	        args: serde_json::Value,
246	        prompt_tokens: u32,
247	        candidates_tokens: u32,
248	    ) -> Vec<u8> {
249	        frame(json!({
250	            "candidates": [{
251	                "content": { "parts": [
252	                    {
253	                        "functionCall": { "name": name, "args": args, "id": call_id },
254	                        "thoughtSignature": THOUGHT_SIGNATURE
255	                    }
256	                ] }
257	            }],
258	            "usageMetadata": {
259	                "promptTokenCount": prompt_tokens,
260	                "candidatesTokenCount": candidates_tokens
261	            }
262	        }))
263	    }

265	    /// The scripted response for one scenario, or `None` for
266	    /// `FragmentedToolName`, which this subject declines.
267	    ///
268	    /// Returning an `Option` rather than panicking on the declined scenario is
269	    /// what lets [`Gemini::encodes_stop_reason`] call this for *every*
270	    /// scenario and measure the bytes — see `bedrock::script`'s doc for the
271	    /// same pattern.
272	    fn script(scenario: Scenario) -> Option<Script> {
273	        // The two-delta opening every text scenario shares. Both deltas carry
274	        // `usageMetadata` — see the module doc's "`usageMetadata` appears on
275	        // every chunk" section for why. Numbers match
276	        // `multi_chunk_usage_emits_usage_per_chunk`'s two chunks verbatim.
277	        let opening = || vec![text_delta("Hel", 1, 1), text_delta("lo", 1, 2)];
278	        // The opening plus one chunk carrying BOTH the stop reason and usage
279	        // — see the module doc for why those two are never split across two
280	        // chunks in this subject.
281	        let through_stop = || {
282	            let mut chunks = opening();
283	            chunks.push(stop_chunk("!", "STOP", 1, 3));
284	            chunks
285	        };
286	
287	        let (chunks, gate_after, ending) = match scenario {
288	            // Full stream: deltas, then the combined stop-reason/usage chunk,
289	            // then the `[DONE]` sentinel and a clean end of body. This is the
290	            // arm that exercises `model.rs`'s `[DONE]` terminal path
291	            // (`model.rs:155-158`) — see the module doc's two-terminal-arms
292	            // section.
293	            Scenario::CleanStop => {
294	                let mut chunks = through_stop();
295	                chunks.push(done());
296	                (chunks, None, Ending::Clean)
297	            }
298	            // The stop reason and usage are observed, then the body simply
299	            // ends — no `[DONE]` anywhere in this script — so the buffered
300	            // stop reason has to be flushed by the bare-EOF arm
301	            // (`model.rs:149-152`), the OTHER terminal path. Together with
302	            // `CleanStop` this is what makes S2 non-vacuous for this subject:
303	            // each scenario exercises a different arm of `model.rs`'s event
304	            // loop, not the same one twice.
305	            Scenario::TruncatedAfterStopReason => (through_stop(), None, Ending::Clean),
306	            // The body ends cleanly mid-generation: no `finishReason` chunk
307	            // ever arrives, so no stop reason is ever observed. The SCRIPT
308	            // shape (a delta, then EOF, no `finishReason`) matches
309	            // `truncated_stream_no_finish`'s envelope
310	            // (`gemini_streaming.rs:60-63`) — `opening()` alone.
311	            Scenario::TruncatedMidGeneration => (opening(), None, Ending::Clean),
312	            // Same prefix, but the connection is torn down without a
313	            // terminating chunk, so the client observes a transport error
314	            // (`model.rs`'s `Some(Err(e))` arm) rather than an end-of-stream.
315	            Scenario::ErrorMidGeneration => (opening(), None, Ending::Abort),
316	            // The stop reason and usage are buffered/observed and *then* the
317	            // body is aborted, so the error path must not flush a `Finish`.
318	            // If `stop_chunk` were ever dropped from this script by mistake,
319	            // this scenario's observable events would collapse to exactly
320	            // `ErrorMidGeneration`'s (`[TokenDelta, Usage, TokenDelta, Usage,
321	            // Err]`, from `opening()`'s two `usageMetadata`-carrying deltas).
322	            // As scripted, `stop_chunk("!", ...)` itself carries a non-empty
323	            // text part alongside its own `usageMetadata`, so it adds one
324	            // more `TokenDelta`/`Usage` pair before the `Err`, not merely a
325	            // trailing `Usage`. [`Gemini::encodes_stop_reason`]'s measured
326	            // scan is what keeps the two distinguishable at the fixture
327	            // level regardless of which of those it is.
328	            Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason => (through_stop(), None, Ending::Abort),
329	            // One content delta goes out, then the server parks holding the
330	            // second back (`gate_after: Some(1)` pauses *before* the chunk at
331	            // index 1, per `server.rs`'s `feed` loop) — no `finishReason`
332	            // chunk anywhere in this script, so no stop reason exists even
333	            // after the gate releases.
334	            Scenario::CancelMidGeneration => (opening(), Some(1), Ending::Clean),
335	            // The stop reason AND its usage are both observed before the gate
336	            // — [`stop_chunk`] carries both in one event, so this scenario
337	            // needs no *extra* usage chunk appended for the gate to sit
338	            // after, the same shape as `anthropic`'s `message_delta`.
339	            //
340	            // **This comment is the only guard for this scenario on this
341	            // subject.** The harness's own "at least one `Usage` observed"
342	            // floor (`assert_conforms`'s `floor_violation`) is VACUOUS here,
343	            // the same way it is for `anthropic`: `text_delta` (module doc,
344	            // "`usageMetadata` appears on every chunk") already emits a
345	            // `Usage` on the very first chunk of `opening()`, so that floor
346	            // is satisfied whether or not the gate sits in the right place —
347	            // even a gate placed before `stop_chunk` would still show a
348	            // `Usage` from the first `text_delta`, and pass. An earlier draft
349	            // of this module confined `usageMetadata` to the stop-reason
350	            // chunk specifically to keep this floor non-vacuous; the live
351	            // capture (module doc) showed that shape does not occur in real
352	            // traffic, so it was removed — fidelity over a convenient floor.
353	            //
354	            // So the only thing standing between this scenario and silently
355	            // degrading into `CancelMidGeneration` under another name is
356	            // this: `gate_after` is a COUNT — `chunks.len()`, not a
357	            // hand-typed literal — read *after* `through_stop()` has pushed
358	            // `stop_chunk` onto `chunks`. That parks the server with
359	            // `stop_chunk` already sent and the body still open, so
360	            // cancellation truncates the stream strictly after the stop
361	            // reason was buffered.
362	            Scenario::CancelAfterStopReason => {
363	                let chunks = through_stop();
364	                let gate_after = chunks.len();
365	                (chunks, Some(gate_after), Ending::Clean)
366	            }
367	            // Declined — see the module doc's "why `FragmentedToolName` is
368	            // declined" section and `Gemini::stream`.
369	            Scenario::FragmentedToolName => return None,
370	            // A whole tool call, transcribed from the live capture (module
371	            // doc, "Live capture"): the name, arguments, id and
372	            // `thoughtSignature` arrive together in one `functionCall` part
373	            // alongside `usageMetadata` and no `finishReason` (see
374	            // [`tool_call_chunk`]'s doc), then a separate chunk carries an
375	            // empty text part, `finishReason: "STOP"`, and `usageMetadata`
376	            // again (see [`stop_chunk`]'s doc on its `text: ""` reuse), then
377	            // the `[DONE]` sentinel — not itself part of the capture, which
378	            // ended at bare EOF (see [`done`]'s doc).
379	            Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop => (
380	                vec![
381	                    tool_call_chunk(TOOL_CALL_ID, TOOL_NAME, json!({ "city": "Berlin" }), 58, 16),
382	                    stop_chunk("", "STOP", 58, 16),
383	                    done(),
384	                ],
385	                None,
386	                Ending::Clean,
387	            ),
388	            // Declined — the scenario serves an anthropic thinking block.
389	            Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop => return None,
390	            // Not served — see the reason in `stream`.
391	            Scenario::ReasoningCleanStop => return None,
392	        };
393	
394	        Some(Script {
395	            content_type: "text/event-stream",
396	            chunks,
397	            gate_after,
398	            ending,
399	        })
400	    }

before the probe results. The Gemini stream and request work waits for the results. If capture 1
shows a different wire shape than this design expects, stop and bring it to Sven. Fixtures are
transcribed from the captures, with each real signature replaced by a placeholder. No real
signature goes into the repo or the PR body. Vertex is not probed; the spec states this limit in the
Gemini README.

### Probe results (2026-11-20)

Sven ran the probe against the Developer API on `gemini-3.8-flash`. No real signature value is
recorded here. Lengths are given.

**Capture 1 (streamed, three parallel calls).** HTTP 200, `finishReason` STOP. The stream has four
SSE chunks. Chunks 0 to 2 each hold one part with one `functionCall`. Chunk 3 holds `{"text": ""}`
with `finishReason: STOP` and no signature. `functionCall.id` is present on every call (native ids
of the form `call_<digits>`). `thoughtSignature` is a sibling of `functionCall` in the same part and
the same chunk. It is on the first call only, and it is 1140 characters long. The other two calls
have no signature. This matches the design.

first to last. So the order risk is real, and the `index` field is needed to restore the order.

final text part. The design ignores it (non-goal).

### Harness (`src/lib.rs`)

  `scenario_all_is_exhaustive`.
- `pub struct ExpectedCall { pub name: &'static str, pub args: &'static str }`, with doc comments.
- The trait method `fn fixture_calls(&self, scenario: Scenario) -> &'static [ExpectedCall];`. It has no
  default.
- `Violation::ToolCallsMismatch { expected: Vec<(String, Value)>, observed: Vec<(String, Value)> }`.
- `floor_violation` has the new last parameter `calls: &[ExpectedCall]`. `assert_conforms_with` passes
  `subject.fixture_calls(scenario)`. The new floors:
  - `ParallelToolCallCleanStop` is in the tool arm, the clean-stop `Finish` floor and the
    `FinishReason` check.
  - Declared-name floor: when `calls` is not empty, every declared name must be on a named
    `ToolCallDelta`. When `calls` is empty, the floor checks `tool_name`, as before.
  - `ReasoningCleanStop` and `ParallelToolCallCleanStop` with empty `calls` fail with
    `InsufficientEvidence("the subject declares no calls ...")`.
  - `ParallelToolCallCleanStop` needs two or more distinct non-blank `call_id`s
    (`"fewer than two distinct non-blank call_ids ..."`).
  - For every scenario with a non-empty `calls`, the new helper `calls_mismatch` runs. It groups the
    deltas by `call_id` in first-seen order, takes the first name, concatenates the `args_delta`s,
    and reads blank or whitespace-only text as `{}`. It compares the groups with the declared calls
    by position, by name and by parsed value. A position whose observed arguments do not parse is
    skipped, so assertion 10 reports it. If the list lengths differ, or a parsed position differs,
    the result is `ToolCallsMismatch`. In that output, an unparseable call shows `null`. A declared
    `args` that does not parse panics, because it is a bug in the subject's table.

  now include that pair, so each test still fails for its own reason only.

- `ExpectedCall` is imported.

  `fixture_finish_reason` returns `None`. `fixture_calls(_)` returns `&[]`.

  `fixture_finish_reason` have the new arm. The new exhaustive `fixture_calls` returns `RUN_C_CALLS`
  for `ReasoningCleanStop` and `&[]` for all other scenarios.
- **R2 (anthropic `ReasoningCleanStop`):**
  - New `RUN_C_TOOL_NAME = "lookup_city_code"` (line 106). The script sends it in the `tool_use` start
    again. The scan test uses it too.
  - `RUN_C_CALLS` = one call, `lookup_city_code`, args `{"city": "Paris"}`. That is the four
    `input_json_delta` fragments of lines 109-118 joined (`""`, `{"city"`, `: "Pari`, `s"}`).
  - `request()` offers `lookup_city_code` (city: string) for `ReasoningCleanStop`, and `get_weather`
    for the two other tool scenarios. The doc says that the run C request is not in the repo. So
    only the tool name comes from the capture. The description string is
    "Return the internal code for a city."
  - Provenance comment: the old edit 2 (the rename) is removed, and the edits are renumbered 1-3. The
    `json!` edit now says: "its key order and spacing can differ from the source. The keys and values

    ended at bare EOF. The provenance comment cites SMA-827 design "Capture 1"

    two edits: the placeholder `SIG_A` was already in the file, and the blank separator lines become
    `\n\n`. A bullet in the module doc's provenance list names the file too.
  - Review Focus 2: I wrote `gemini_parallel_script_encodes_its_stop_reason` first. It failed (RED
    below). Then I made the marker change: `FINISH_REASON_MARKERS` holds the compact form and the
    spaced form (`"finishReason": "`), and `has_finish_reason` scans for both.
    `scan_finds_only_a_populated_finish_reason` now also asserts that Capture 1's stop chunk matches,
    and that its three `functionCall` chunks do not.
  - `request()` offers `search` (q: string) and `weather` (city: string).

  form.

   leave out `thoughtSignature`, and it also prefers the marker change "because it keeps the bytes
   faithful". These two items conflict. A `json!` builder writes compact JSON and drops the
   capture's `role`, `index`, `totalTokenCount`, `modelVersion` and `responseId` fields, unless every
   field becomes a parameter. Also, a `json!`-built stop chunk has no space, so the marker test would
   pass at once and could not be RED. So I send the four captured payloads byte for byte, and I did
   not add the builder. Because of this, trap 2 (the signature on call 1 only) is met by the bytes

   name at that position is not reported by the floor. Assertion 10 still fails the stream, because
